teide.desc: Spain's highest peak at 3,715 m. UNESCO World Heritage. Cable car takes you near the summit.

anaga.desc: Ancient laurel forest. Stunning landscapes and cliff-top trails.

icod.desc: Canary Islands' oldest tree, over 800 years old. Icod village and traditional wineries nearby.

montana-roja.desc: Reddish volcanic cone and Special Nature Reserve next to El Médano. Easy 45-minute ascent with panoramic views of the entire south and La Gomera. Very photogenic at sunset.

acantilados-gigantes.desc: Spain's most impressive cliffs up to 600 m high. The most spectacular way to see them is by boat. Habitat of dolphins and pilot whales year-round.

bosque-esperanza.desc: Pine forest and laurel forest along the Cumbre Dorsal. Mystical mist, trails through Canarian pines and Jardina Viewpoint. Endemic bird watching area.

riscos-chio.desc: Black lava field created by the 1798 Chío volcano eruption. Trail through lava flows and otherworldly scenery. Teide views from Chío Viewpoint.

mirador-pino-galdo.desc: Secret viewpoint in Anaga with Atlantic Ocean and massif views. Surrounded by laurel forest. Very peaceful and uncrowded.

mirador-la-ruleta.desc: Panoramic viewpoint inside Teide National Park, by the TF-21. Spectacular views of Teide and Las Cañadas. Easy car access. Especially magical at sunrise.

teresitas.aviso: Access on the TF-11 from Santa Cruz. Bus 910 every 10-15 min at peak times: first around 5:00, last around 23:00.
teresitas.desc: Tenerife's most beautiful urban beach. Saharan golden sand, palm trees and calm waters. Red Cross lifeguards all year.

el-duque.desc: Exclusive beach of fine pale sand in Costa Adeje, 390 m long with turquoise water. Five-star hotels, upmarket restaurants and straw parasols. Blue Flag. ⚠️ Open to the Atlantic with no breakwaters: waves are stronger in the afternoon and the bottom drops away quickly as you go in. Lifeguards from 10:00 to 18:00. Street parking is very hard: better the underground car parks at The Corner Adeje or Plaza del Duque, under 3 min on foot. Buses 467, 471 and 473, El Duque stop.

benijo.desc: Black volcanic sand with rock stacks. Wild and rugged, perfect for photography. Lifeguard in summer only.

el-medano.desc: European capital of windsurfing and kitesurfing. Long beach with steady winds and Montaña Roja. Also listed in some official registers as Playa de Leocadio Machado.

bollullo.desc: ⚠️ The access footpath suffers intermittent temporary closures due to rockfall risk on the cliffs: check its status before heading down. Black sand between green cliffs. Access via trail. Strong swell almost all year round: take extra care when swimming.

playa-los-patos.desc: ⚠️ Access officially closed and fenced off: the old stairway is impassable and the cliff paths are steep and dangerous; anyone going down does so at their own risk. Big wild black-sand beach of about 700 m beneath the El Rincón cliffs in La Orotava, next to El Bollullo. The north’s classic naturist beach: no services, strong surf and currents. No parking of its own.

las-vistas.desc: Large family beach with promenade. Calm waters ideal for children. Red Cross lifeguards all year. Blue Flag 2026.

playa-americas.desc: South tourism hub. Golden sand, warm waters and lively atmosphere. Permanent lifeguard service.

san-juan.desc: Quiet and authentic fishing village beach. Fresh fish restaurants. Blue Flag 2026.

alcala.desc: Small black sand cove with crystal-clear water. Authentic fishing village. No crowds, no lifeguard.

abama.desc: One of the most exclusive beaches. Golden sand and crystal waters next to Abama hotel.

arena.desc: Fine black sand beach in the centre of Puerto de Santiago, 140 m long and about 40 m wide. Blue Flag for decades. One of the least windy and warmest spots on the island, sheltered from the trade wind. ⚠️ But it faces the open sea: there are currents and moderate to strong waves with a significant undertow. Swim with care and always follow the lifeguard's flag. Lifeguard posts, showers, footbaths, toilets and sunbed hire. Ramps and wooden walkways for wheelchairs and prams. Views of La Gomera and the Los Gigantes cliffs. Bus stop La Arena (7232) right by the beach. The direct 477 from Costa Adeje starts around 5:30, and the last one back from Los Gigantes leaves around 20:40.

playa-socorro.desc: North surfers' favourite. Powerful waves, black sand and local vibe. Blue Flag 2026.

tejita.desc: ⚠️ Dogs prohibited by municipal by-law, subject to fines. Tenerife's largest natural beach next to Montaña Roja. Golden sand and nudist area.

fanabe.desc: Family beach in Costa Adeje with full services. Adapted access for babies.

playa-jardin.desc: Designed by César Manrique. Black sand, native plant gardens, waterfalls and Teide views.

san-marcos.desc: ⚠️ Historic Icod beach that has lost much of its black sand to storms and currents after the breakwater works: pebbles now abound. Natural cove sheltered by cliffs in Icod. Black sand, calm waters. Blue Flag 2026.

almaciga.desc: Wild beach in Taganana with black sand and gravel. Strong swell. Lifeguard in summer only.

charco-viento.desc: Iconic volcanic natural pools in La Guancha. Crystal water and wild black rock scenery.

punta-hidalgo.desc: Natural pools in the northeast. Volcanic landscape where the Atlantic forms sheltered tide pools.

charco-abrigos.desc: Calm natural pool at Costa del Silencio. Very clear waters. Fresh fish restaurants nearby.

el-pris.desc: North's best-kept secret in fishing village El Pris (Tacoronte). Crystal waters in a totally local atmosphere.

mesa-mar.desc: Tacoronte natural pools with cooler crystal water. Volcanic setting right by the village.

charco-laja.desc: Black volcanic rock natural pools in San Juan de la Rambla. Very popular with northern locals. Clean and deep water, ideal for jumping from the rocks. Festive atmosphere in summer.

charco-diablo.desc: Spectacular volcanic natural pools in Buenavista del Norte. Access via cliff-side trail. Very blue waters and completely wild surroundings. Only for calm sea days.

charco-verde-guancha.desc: Natural pool on the coast of La Guancha, in the Punta de Marrero area, next to two equally spectacular rock pools: La Arena and El Viento. Volcanic landscape among banana plantations, with Teide behind, a sheer cliff and the ocean. There is no road to it: park by the plantations in the coastal neighbourhood of Santa Catalina and walk down an unsignposted path. The pool sits above the sea and only renews its water in heavy swell. Do not go down when the northern sea is rough, or without grippy footwear: the last stretch over volcanic rock is steep and slippery.

masca.aviso: Limited roadside spaces with a strict rule: 2 hours maximum between 08:00 and 14:00, or you risk a fine.
masca.desc: Hidden mountain village. The gorge ends at a spectacular virgin beach.

observatorio.desc: World's best solar observatory. Day visits and night astrotourism. Starlight destination.

roques-garcia.desc: Teide National Park's most visited trail. 3.5 km circular, 2 hours, easy with some elevation. Starts at the Parador. Loops around the spectacular Roques de García (the famous 'Roque Cinchado' was on the old 1000-peseta banknote). Views of Teide, the Caldera, and viewpoint over Llano de Ucanca. Buses 348/342. Large free parking.

montana-blanca.desc: The official starting point for hiking to Teide summit (3,715 m). Trail 10 (TF-6) from 2,350 m. Free permit required for the final 200 m. Full ascent takes 5–7 hours. Impressive and demanding experience.

ruta-pico-viejo.desc: Teide's twin crater at 3,135 m. Circular trail along the crater rim with unique views. Less crowded than Teide. No special permit required. One of the best routes in the National Park.

cumbre-dorsal.desc: Tenerife's backbone at over 1,000 m. TF-24 road through Canarian pine forests with mystical mist. La Jardina viewpoint with views of Teide and both coasts.

sendero-la-orotava.desc: Historic royal path linking La Orotava to Teide. 18 km continuous ascent through pine forest and plateau. The same path used by the Guanches to reach the sacred summit. Good physical condition required.

ruta-anaga-taganana.desc: Anaga's most spectacular trail linking Taganana to Almáciga via the ridges. Laurel forest, Atlantic views and picture-perfect villages. Moderate, 3 hours return.

ruta-masca-playa.desc: ⚠️ Access regulated by the Cabildo: advance booking on its official website and approved mountain footwear are mandatory. The jetty is closed to recreational boats, so the trail must be hiked both down and back up. Tenerife's most famous and spectacular hiking route. 3 hours descending through the gorge to Masca's virgin beach. Boat pick-up included at the end. Booking required. Only in organised groups.

sendero-sentidos.desc: Anaga's most popular and accessible trail. Three short circular routes (340 m, 540 m, 1.3 km) starting from the Cruz del Carmen Visitor Centre. Trail 1 is wheelchair and pushchair accessible. Laurel forest with sensory panels (touch, smell, look). Suitable for all ages. Free parking. Buses 76, 77, 273, 275 (Cruz del Carmen stop 2232).

sendero-pijaral.desc: ⚠️ FREE PERMIT REQUIRED at centralreservas.tenerife.es (45 people/day). 6.7 km circular trail through El Pijaral Integral Natural Reserve, in the heart of Anaga. Tertiary-relic laurel forest, pijara ferns up to 3 m. Cabezo del Tejo viewpoint over Taganana. Medium difficulty, 3 hours. Start at La Ensillada car park (TF-123).

sendero-afur-taganana.desc: ⚠️ OFFICIAL NOTICE: PR-TF 8 may be closed for maintenance. Check tenerifeon.es/incidencias before setting out. · Demanding 14 km circular route, 5-6 hours. Starts in the village of Afur (under 100 residents), crosses the Tamadiste ravine down to the coast, climbs to Taganana and returns through monteverde forest. Combines ravines, laurel forest, coastal cliffs and picturesque villages. For experienced hikers. Bring water and food.

sendero-guajara.desc: The highest summit of Las Cañadas (2,718 m) excluding Teide. 11 km round trip, 5 hours. Start at the Cañadas Parador. Trail 5 to Degollada de Guajara, then a demanding final ascent with spectacular views of Teide and the whole Caldera. No permit needed. Bring plenty of water (no fountains), sun protection, jacket (cold at summit).

sendero-pico-viejo.desc: One of Teide's most demanding routes. 20 km round trip, 7-8 hours. Start at the Sanatorio car park. Ascends to the Pico Viejo crater (3,135 m), with lunar landscapes of black and red lava flows. No cable car, all on foot. Only for experienced hikers in good shape. Best April-June. Bring lots of water, food, warm clothing and start very early.

sendero-teno-baracan.desc: Beautiful circular route in Teno Rural Park. ~10 km, 4 hours. Starts in Teno Alto village (goat farms, artisanal cheese makers) and climbs Pico Baracán (1,002 m) with spectacular views of Teide and La Gomera, La Palma, El Hierro on clear days. Crosses fayal-heath and laurel forest unique at this altitude. Medium difficulty. Bar and shop in Teno Alto.

sendero-chinyero.desc: Easy and unique circular route around Chinyero volcano, Tenerife's last eruption (1909). 6 km, 2-3 hours, almost no elevation. Start at Arenas Negras car park (Santiago del Teide). Passes still-visible black lava flows, pine forests and Teide views. Family-friendly. Some shaded areas. Year-round except very windy days.

prtf-1-mercedes-cruz-carmen.desc: Historic ascent from Las Mercedes village (La Laguna) to the Cruz del Carmen visitor centre, along an old royal path through laurel forest. 4 km one-way, 2.5 hours, +500 m elevation gain. Medium difficulty due to constant climb. Connects to the Anaga trail network. TITSA buses to Las Mercedes.

prtf-2-taborno-pico-ingles.desc: Spectacular ridge route between Taborno and Pico del Inglés viewpoint (992 m), descending to Valle Seco. 11 km, 5 hours, demanding elevation. Exceptional views of Anaga massif, north and south coasts on clear days. Experienced hikers only. Connects with PR-TF 2.1 (El Frontón).

prtf-4-bailadero-taganana.desc: Descent from El Bailadero (Anaga ridge) towards Taganana, a coastal village from the 15th century. 5 km, 2 hours, steep descent. Crosses laurel forest and ends with views of the Roques de Anaga. Possible bus return from Taganana. Historic path used by fishermen to reach the mountain markets.

prtf-5-chamorga-igueste.desc: East-end Anaga trail, one of Tenerife's most pristine areas. 9 km, 4 hours. Starts at the isolated hamlet of Chamorga (one of the island's most remote villages) and descends to Igueste de San Andrés along the north Anaga coast. Wild goats, palm groves, cliffs. Experienced hikers only.

prtf-6-3-benijo-draguillo.desc: One of Tenerife's most highly rated routes (4.7★ with 2,000+ reviews). 8.4 km, 2.5-3 hours. Starts at the legendary Benijo beach and climbs old rural paths to El Draguillo hamlet. Spectacular views of the Roques de Anaga, wild coast and laurel forests. Medium-high difficulty.

prtf-10-cruz-carmen-chinamada.desc: ⚠️ Chinamada-Punta del Hidalgo section under works (Mon-Fri 7-15:30). Classic trail from Cruz del Carmen to the troglodyte hamlet of Chinamada (inhabited cave houses), one of Anaga's ethnographic gems. 8.5 km one-way, 3.5 hours. Crosses deep laurel forest and spectacular viewpoints. Possible to continue to Punta del Hidalgo (PR-TF 11 variant). Buses 76, 77, 273.

sendero-bosque-enigmas.desc: Very popular Anaga loop, ~5 km, 2 hours, easy. Starts at Zapata viewpoint or Cruz del Carmen and crosses 'magical' laurel forests with century-old trees, mist and moss. Suitable for families with older children. Good TF-12 access. Bring a jacket — Anaga is humid and cool even in summer.

sendero-roque-bodegas.desc: Short and easy coastal walk between Almáciga and Roque de las Bodegas villages, at the end of TF-134 on Anaga's north coast. ~2 km round trip, 1 hour. Views of the iconic Roque de las Bodegas and wild beaches. Fresh fish restaurants at both ends. Ideal combined with Benijo beach.

prtf-6-chamorga-roque-bermejo.desc: Iconic circular route at the far northeast of Anaga. 13.5 km, 5-6 hours. Starts in the last car-accessible village (Chamorga, paved in 1975) and descends to remote Roque Bermejo (almost-abandoned fishing hamlet), continuing via El Draguillo and back. Combines coast, ravines, palm grove and laurel forest. Bus line 947 from Santa Cruz (limited days). ⚠️ Slippery sections near cliffs.

prtf-6-1-chamorga-faro-anaga.desc: Variant trail to Faro de Anaga (1864, the island's oldest lighthouse). 3.2 km one-way, 1h 40min. Starts in Chamorga next to Bar Casa Álvaro. Climbs via Casas de Tafada with a self-guided 7-point QR trail. Views of Roque Pilón and the open Atlantic. Combinable with PR-TF 6 for a loop. Suitable for beginner hikers.

prtf-9-afur-carboneras.desc: Short and beautiful trail between two villages of under 100 inhabitants in the heart of Anaga. 4 km one-way, 1h 30min, moderate difficulty. Crosses Las Carboneras ravine, monteverde and laurel forest. Las Carboneras preserves cave-houses (troglodyte homes). Connects with PR-TF 8 (Afur-Taganana) and PR-TF 10.1.

prtf-11-cruz-carmen-batan.desc: The great north-south traverse of Anaga, alternative to PR-TF 10. 14 km one-way, 5-6 hours. From Cruz del Carmen down to El Batán hamlet (inhabited caves) and on to Punta del Hidalgo coast. Spectacular views of Roque de Dos Hermanos. High difficulty due to elevation. Return bus from Punta del Hidalgo. Lunch at Las Bodegas de El Batán.

sendero-samara.desc: Easy circular route with spectacular lunar landscapes. 5 km, 2 hours. Start at Mirador de Samara car park (TF-38). Loops around Montaña de Samara, a volcanic cone of red and black sands. Views of Teide, Pico Viejo and the lava flows of Teide's last eruption (1798). No shade: bring water and sun protection. Perfect at sunset.

gr131-tramo1-esperanza-caldera.desc: First stage of the GR-131 Grand Route that crosses the entire island. 14 km, 5 hours. Starts at La Esperanza village (cumbre dorsal, 850 m) and goes through protected pine forest to La Caldera recreational area (Aguamansa). Canary pine forests, characteristic mystic mist. Marked trail, white and red. Medium difficulty. Day stage. Bus from La Esperanza.

gr131-tramo5-vilaflor-arona.desc: Final GR-131 stage in Tenerife, arriving at the tourist south. 12 km, 4 hours, almost entirely downhill. From Vilaflor (1,400 m) to Arona village (610 m). Canary pine forest at the start, then scrubland of tabaibas and euphorbias. Views of La Gomera. Close of the island route that started in La Esperanza. Bus 482/417 from Arona.

sendero-barranco-infierno.desc: ⚠️ MANDATORY BOOKING at barrancodelinfierno.es (300 people/day, €11). The most visited route in the south. 6.5 km round trip, 3.5 hours. Entrance in Adeje town centre. Follows 'Hell's Gorge' to Tenerife's highest waterfall (80 m). Helmet mandatory (provided). Not suitable for under-5s. Guanche caves along the way. Closed on rainy or windy days. Bring water and hiking shoes.

sendero-prtf-72-paisaje-lunar.desc: Trail to the iconic Lunar Landscape, unique formations of eroded white pumice. 13.4 km circular, 4 hours, +600 m elevation. Starts in Vilaflor. Crosses Canary pine forest and ravine to reach the spectacular landscape. ⚠️ SEASONAL CLOSURES for mouflon control (April-June, Oct-Nov, 7am-4pm). Check tenerifeon.es before going. Must-do.

sendero-roque-conde.desc: Iconic volcanic mesa in the south, symbol of Arona (1,001 m). 7.5 km circular from Vento de Arona, 3 hours, +410 m elevation. Spectacular views over the ocean and tourist resorts. Flat summit where Guanches of the Abona kingdom lived (archaeological sites). Final climb very steep with ropes. Dry trail — bring lots of water. Best in winter due to sun.

sendero-prtf-51-punta-teno.desc: Historic trail to the island's most remote lighthouse. 11 km one-way, 4 hours. Crosses the Teno tunnel (torch recommended) and descends via Camino del Risco to Punta de Teno. ⚠️ Since 1 Jan 2025: Punta de Teno access restricted 10am-7pm (bus only). Trail open but no car access during those hours. Views of La Gomera and La Palma.

sendero-prtf-58-camino-risco.desc: Old lighthouse keepers' path with vertiginous descent through Teno cliffs. 10.5 km, 4.5-5 hours, -684 m descent. Starts at Plaza Los Bailaderos (Teno Alto), zigzags down to Buenavista. Once the only access to Punta de Teno. Combinable with PR-TF 51 for full route. For experienced hikers. Hard on the knees. Return bus from Buenavista.

pr-tf-3-chinamada.desc: Trail leading to Chinamada hamlet in Anaga Rural Park, one of the most unique inhabited settlements in the Canary Islands: around 30 cave houses carved into the rock that are still lived in today. Most common access is from Punta del Hidalgo (PR-TF 10, Chinamada section) or from Las Carboneras. Chinamada has a small chapel, a native Pedigüey sheep farm and spectacular views of Anaga's ravines. The Mirador de Aguaide (400m from the hamlet) is unmissable. Difficulty: Medium-High. Experienced hikers only. Bring water.

gr131-tramo2-portillo-guajara.desc: GR-131 Anaga-Chasna section 2. From El Portillo Visitor Centre (TF-21 km 32, 2,030 m) along the ancient Royal Chasna Path through Las Siete Cañadas to Degollada de Guajara (2,715 m). Distance ~14 km. Difficulty High. Protected area: no camping or straying from path.
gr131-tramo2-portillo-guajara.cat: GR-131 · Section 2 · Las Siete Cañadas · Teide · High

gr131-tramo3-guajara-vilaflor.desc: GR-131 section 3. From Degollada de Guajara (2,715 m) through the Lunar Landscape and Vilaflor's pine forests to the village (1,400 m). Descent of 1,300 m in ~12 km. The trail passes the start of PR-TF 72 (Lunar Landscape). Vilaflor is Tenerife's highest inhabited village. Difficulty High.

pr-tf-52-monte-agua.desc: PR-TF-52 Monte del Agua is one of the most spectacular and least crowded laurel forest trails in Tenerife, in Teno Rural Park. It starts in the hamlet of Erjos (Los Silos municipality) and runs through the dense laurel forest of Monte del Agua to Las Portelas, with option to continue to El Palmar. Distance: 10.5km. Difficulty: Low (gentle slope almost all the way). Max altitude: ~1,100m. Primary laurel forest with endemic Bolle's pigeon and white-tailed laurel pigeon, follao, viñátigo, til, holly and large heathers. Spectacular viewpoint at Mesita del Hurto over the forest. Teide views from the higher areas. Very few people compared to Anaga trails.
pr-tf-52-monte-agua.cat: PR-TF-52 · Laurel Forest · Monte del Agua · Teno · Low

golf-abama.desc: One of Europe's best golf courses according to the Golf Digest Editors Choice Award (5 consecutive times). 18 holes Par 72, 6,271 m, designed by Dave Thomas. At the Ritz-Carlton Abama Resort (Guía de Isora), with 23 lakes, waterfalls and 25,000 palm trees. Atlantic and La Gomera views. GPS buggies included. Unlimited driving range, putting green, golf academy. Max handicap: 28 men / 36 women. Hours: 7:30-19:30. High season green fee around 145 €. A benchmark of European golf.
golf-abama.cat: Golf · 18 Holes · Par 72 · Guía de Isora · Luxury

golf-buenavista.desc: Golf course designed by Severiano Ballesteros in the far northwest of Tenerife. 18-hole Par 72, 6,150m. Spectacular natural setting next to the ocean and Teno Natural Park. Several holes border the cliff with the sensation of hitting directly into the sea. Lakes on holes 9 and 18. Golf academy. Meliá Hacienda del Conde 5* hotel integrated. High season green fee: €90-140. Tel: 922 129 034.
golf-buenavista.cat: Golf · 18 Holes · Par 72 · Buenavista · Seve Ballesteros

golf-amarilla.desc: Golf course designed by Donald Steel, next to Marina San Miguel. 18-hole Par 72. Famous for its hole 5, where you must hit over the ocean to reach the green — one of Spain's most iconic holes. Fairways bordering the volcanic coast. Teide and Atlantic views. Golf academy, driving range, putting green, pro shop. South Tenerife.
golf-amarilla.cat: Golf · 18 Holes · Par 72 · San Miguel · Volcanic Coast

golf-del-sur.desc: Historic south Tenerife golf course designed by José Gancedo, expanded over the years. 27 holes (3 x 9-hole courses: North, South and Links). Par 72 for 18 holes. Has hosted the Tenerife Open on the European Tour. Unique volcanic setting with Teide and Atlantic views. Complex with apartments and hotels. Golf academy. South of the island, near Reina Sofía Airport.
golf-del-sur.cat: Golf · 27 Holes · San Miguel · European Tour

golf-costa-adeje.desc: Golf course in Adeje, opened in 1998. 27 holes (3 x 9-hole courses: Sea, Lake and Mountain). Par 72 for 18 holes. Venue for the BMW Golf Cup International World Final (1999). Designed by Pepe Gancedo. Teide, La Gomera and Atlantic views. Golf academy, driving range. Next to Fañabé, easily accessible from Costa Adeje and Las Américas.

golf-las-americas.desc: 18-hole Par 72 golf course next to Playa de las Américas. Designed by Folco Nardi. Ocean and La Gomera views. Privileged position in the heart of the south tourist zone. Club rental, buggies, golf academy. One of the most accessible courses in the south of the island for tourists.
golf-las-americas.cat: Golf · 18 Holes · Par 72 · Las Américas · South

rcg-tenerife.desc: Tenerife's oldest golf course and one of Spain's most historic, founded in 1932 (with predecessors since 1896). 18-hole Par 71, 5,740m. In San Lázaro (La Laguna), surrounded by native woodland. Classic course with all holes individually named. Member fees and visitor green fees. Advance booking essential.
rcg-tenerife.cat: Golf · Royal Club · 18 Holes · Par 71 · La Laguna · 1932

golf-los-palos.desc: Pitch & putt and short 9-hole course in Arona (south Tenerife), Ctra. Guaza-Las Galletas km 7. Ideal for beginners, families and players wanting to practise their short game. Full practice area: chipping green, bunker and putting green. Terrace with views. Quiet and family atmosphere. No age or handicap restrictions. Very accessible from Los Cristianos y Las Américas.

golf-los-lagos.desc: 9-hole Par 33, 2,223m golf course in Costa Adeje. Surrounded by 5 water hazards with streams and a spectacular waterfall. Mix of easy holes and more technical holes defended by bunkers and lakes. Privileged natural setting in west Tenerife. Suitable for all levels.
golf-los-lagos.cat: Golf · 9 Holes · Par 33 · Costa Adeje · West

mirador-pico-ingles.desc: Anaga's most impressive viewpoint at 992 m. 360° views over the whole island, north coast and ocean. Often above the clouds. Car access via TF-12.

candelaria.desc: Shrine of the Patron of the Canary Islands. Nine statues of menceyes (Guanche kings) on the square.

tacoronte.desc: Oldest wine denomination in the Canary Islands. Wineries with unique red and white wines.

siam-park.desc: World's best water park. Giant waves, Tower of Dragon, white sand beach.

jungle-park.desc: Zoological park of 7.5 ha with over 500 animals: white tigers, lions, jaguars, leopards, orangutans, gibbons, chimpanzees, lemurs and penguins. Spectacular free-flight shows with eagles and birds of prey. In Arona.

nucleo-los-cristianos.desc: Heart of the south. Beaches, nightlife, restaurants. 365 days of sun.

corona-forestal.desc: The most extensive natural park in the Canary Islands. Canarian pines, trails and unique Teide views.

paisaje-lunar.desc: Los Escurriales: delicate columns and turrets of white pumice sculpted by erosion above the Vilaflor pine forest, beside the historic Camino de Chasna. A corner that evokes the surface of the Moon, unique in Tenerife. No road access: on foot only via the PR-TF 72 (13.4 km loop from Vilaflor). Protected area: admire it from its viewpoints without stepping on the formations. Sun-exposed with no shade: bring water and sun protection.

malpais-guimar.desc: Protected Natural Space on Tenerife's east coast. Volcanic lava flow field between 1,000 and 2,000 years old reaching the sea, forming a unique black rock coastline. Habitat of the Canarian lizard and various endemic plants. Close to the Güímar Pyramids. Free access via local paths.
malpais-guimar.cat: Natural Space · Güímar · Volcanic · East Coast

jardin-botanico-puerto-cruz.desc: The oldest botanical garden in the Canary Islands and second oldest in Spain, founded in 1788 by Royal Order of King Charles III. In Puerto de la Cruz (Calle Retama 2), with over 5,000 tropical and subtropical species and century-old trees over 40m tall. Cultural Heritage Site since 1994. Hours: 09:00–18:00 (closed 1 Jan, Good Friday, 25 Dec). Entry: €3. Walkable from Puerto de la Cruz centre.
jardin-botanico-puerto-cruz.cat: Botanical Garden · Puerto de la Cruz · 1788 · €3

lajiales-fasnia.desc: Volcanic lava field on Tenerife's east coast, Fasnia municipality. Protected Natural Space of great geological and scenic value. Expanse of historic lava flows reaching the sea, forming a uniquely black coastline with small coves and natural rock pools. Habitat of the Canarian lizard and marine fauna. Free access from Fasnia's coast. Spectacular for volcanic landscape photography.

mirador-teide.desc: The most impressive viewpoint in the National Park, at 2,356 m next to the Cable Car station. 360° views of the crater, Las Cañadas and the whole island. Starting point for the cable car and summit trails.

mirador-punta-homem.desc: Anaga visitor centre. Spectacular viewpoint over the sea and laurel forest.

mirador-maska.desc: Stunning views of the ravine and Masca village nestled between mountains.

mirador-teresitas.desc: ⚠️ The official viewpoint structure is closed for safety reasons (poor condition); the sides of the old road to Igueste are still used for the famous beach photo. Panoramic views over the golden sand beach. The contrast of the beach with San Andrés village is unique.

montana-pelada.desc: Special Nature Reserve next to El Médano and Montaña Roja. Fossil dune of consolidated sand formed thousands of years ago. The ascent rewards with unique views over the La Bocayna Strait and La Gomera on the horizon. Fragile ecosystem of endemic Canarian plants. Short and moderate climb, ideal at dawn.

montana-amarilla.desc: Absolutely unique golden-sulfur coloured volcanic cone in Tenerife. Located in Costa del Silencio, its yellow walls contrast spectacularly with the deep blue of the Atlantic. Marine Reserve with waters rich in colourful fish. The sunset from its summit is breathtakingly beautiful. Free access and just a 20-minute climb.

montana-guaza.desc: The great guardian of southern Tenerife at 427 m. Special Nature Reserve dominating Los Cristianos and Las Américas. Circular 2-hour trail through a semi-arid landscape of tabaibas and cardones. At the summit, a 360° panorama stretching from Teide to La Gomera, El Hierro and La Palma on clear days. A natural viewpoint tourists don't expect to find.

llano-ucanca.desc: The most awe-inspiring plain in Teide National Park. A sea of black volcanic sand surrounded by mountains with Teide in the background. At dawn it fills with impossible oranges and purples. The silence here is absolute, almost sacred. The same landscape that amazed Humboldt and the first European explorers. Accessible by car, no effort needed.

caldeira-canadas.desc: The oldest and most monumental volcanic caldera in Tenerife, 17 km across. The secret heart of the National Park. Formed millions of years ago by the collapse of the ancient stratovolcano. This is where the Guanche legends of Echeyde were born. Its 600 m vertical walls enclose a unique ecosystem where only high-mountain plants grow. One of the most impressive landscapes in all of Macaronesia.

mirador-ruleta-canadas.desc: The most secret and spectacular viewpoint in Las Cañadas del Teide. Direct view of Pico Viejo and the southwest flank of Teide, the most rugged and least photographed. Ideal for contemplating the volcano's grandeur without crowds. At sunset the golden light turns the lavas magical red-orange. Parking by the TF-21 road.

montana-taco.desc: Small volcanic cone in the heart of La Laguna municipality. An unexpected green lung in the middle of the city. Its slopes are covered in monteverde vegetation and offer surprising views of the airport, La Laguna and the northeast coast. Easy 45-minute trail, ideal for a quiet getaway from the city.

pico-teide-cumbre.desc: The summit of Pico del Teide (3,715m) is the highest point in Spain, the highest point of any Atlantic island and the third highest volcano in the world from its oceanic base. The summit is reached on foot from La Rambleta (upper cable car station, 3,555m) via the Telesforo Bravo Trail: 45-minute ascent, easy but demanding at altitude. Free permit required — book on the Teide National Park website months in advance (very limited places). At the summit: sulphurous fumaroles, views to all seven Canary Islands on clear days, and the unique sensation of being at Spain's highest point. Temperature can drop below 0°C. Warm clothing essential.

piscinas-garachico.desc: Lava pools formed by the 1706 Trevejo volcano eruption. Free and spectacular.

piscinas-bajamar.desc: Two large natural pools in the north. Cool water and gentle waves. Authentic local atmosphere.

piscinas-poris.desc: Small natural pools in the south-east. Very peaceful little fishing village.

piscinas-muelle.desc: Natural pool in Puerto de la Cruz next to the harbour. Protected waters and free entry.

charco-chochos.desc: One of the most appreciated natural pools in north Tenerife, in Los Silos municipality. Semi-natural, improved by locals with steps and areas for towels. Walk from Puertito de Los Silos via the La Síbora coastal path (5 min). Crystal clear water, low danger, usable at both low and high tide. Ideal for families. Quiet setting with few tourists. Bring water shoes. Free parking at the port.
charco-chochos.cat: Natural Pool · Los Silos · North · Free

charco-faro-buenavista.desc: Natural pool beside the Buenavista del Norte Lighthouse, at the far northwest tip of Tenerife. Also known as Charco El Rayo for its unusual shape — thought by some to be caused by a lightning strike, but more likely volcanic erosion. Large pool with crystal clear water and impressive views of the Teno Rural Park and coastline. Access via coastal trail from Puertito de Los Silos (30 min) or from Buenavista. Caution: loose stones when entering. Calm seas only.
charco-faro-buenavista.cat: Natural Pool · Buenavista del Norte · Northwest

piscina-jover-tejina.desc: Natural pool on the coast of Tejina (La Laguna municipality), 20 km from Santa Cruz. Quiet and family-friendly with views of Punta del Hidalgo Lighthouse, Bajamar and Mesa de Tejina. Formed by volcanic lava flows. Rectangular pool ~33 m long. Steps to the sea, natural freshwater shower channelled from the mountain, terrace and sunbathing area. Accessible for reduced mobility. Public car park and Tejina Nautical Club nearby. Access via TF-154 from TF-5 exit 11.
piscina-jover-tejina.cat: Natural Pool · Tejina · La Laguna · Accessible

piscinas-alcala-jaquita.desc: The Alcalá Natural Pools, known as Charcos La Jaquita, are one of the most complete natural bathing complexes in south Tenerife, in Guía de Isora municipality. Natural volcanic rocks form a long pool protected from waves next to Playa La Jaquita (black sand). 2km coastal promenade, full facilities: changing rooms, showers, toilets, kiosk, children's area, basketball and volleyball court, lifeguard in high season. Water access steps and safety bars. Free parking next to Hotel Gran Meliá Isora. Crystal clear water, temperature 19-24°C. Suitable for all the family.
piscinas-alcala-jaquita.cat: Natural Pool · Alcalá · Guía de Isora · West · Families

bano-valleseco.desc: Rocky bathing area with pontoons on Avenida de Anaga, next to the Dársena Pesquera fishing harbour in Santa Cruz. It is not a sandy beach: you enter the water from platforms and steps over the rock. Used mainly by locals. Check the sea state and the tide before going down.
bano-valleseco.cat: Rock Bathing · Santa Cruz · Not a sandy beach

playa-san-juan-bajamar.desc: Beach of stones and boulders in Bajamar, not soft sand. Reached on foot down a steep staircase from the upper level. Strong swell, popular with surfers. No services and no lifeguard. Mind the tide: as it rises it leaves very little room.

playa-arenisco.desc: Small beach of rock and black sand in Punta del Hidalgo, right beside the natural pools. Lava flows reach the sea and form tide pools. There is a seafront promenade with restaurants alongside, and toilets, changing rooms and showers in the area. A weekend gathering spot for local families.
playa-arenisco.cat: Beach and Tide Pools · Punta del Hidalgo

playa-arenal-bajamar.desc: Black sand wedged beneath the cliff in Bajamar. Reached by the path from the abandoned Hotel Neptuno, with steps down and no upkeep, and a stretch of boulders before the sand. A surf spot: there is a lateral current and the waves break chaotically near the shore. No services and no lifeguard.
playa-arenal-bajamar.cat: Black Sand under the Cliff · Bajamar

playa-los-troches.desc: Made entirely of boulders and large stone, east of Punta del Hidalgo. Not suitable for swimming: there is submerged rock and the swell is strong. The access is not obvious and you have to pick your way over the stones. Near the end of the Chinamada trail. No facilities of any kind.
playa-los-troches.cat: Boulder Beach · Punta del Hidalgo · Not for swimming

auditorio.desc: Masterpiece by Santiago Calatrava. Symbol of Tenerife. Classical music concerts and opera.

piramides-guimar.desc: Mysterious stepped pyramids discovered by Thor Heyerdahl. Ethnographic museum.

iglesia-concepcion.desc: The oldest church in Santa Cruz, founded in 1502 by the conquerors. Houses the original Cross of the Conquest. Five-storey tower declared an Asset of Cultural Interest. The first stone was laid by Alonso Fernández de Lugo himself.

castillo-negro.desc: Black 17th-century castle. Protected the port of Santa Cruz. Now a cultural centre.

museo-naturaleza.desc: Guanche mummy collection. Volcanic geology and Canarian natural history.

casa-balcones.desc: 17th-century manor house in La Orotava. Typical Canarian carved wood balconies, flower-filled courtyard and local crafts. One of Tenerife's most photographed historic buildings.

cueva-viento.desc: Europe's longest lava tube at over 18 km. Formed 27,000 years ago by Teide lava flows. Limited guided tours. Advance booking essential.

tea-tenerife.desc: Santa Cruz contemporary art centre designed by Herzog & de Meuron. Temporary exhibitions, library, photographic archive and creative workshops.

castillo-san-felipe.desc: 17th-century fortress that defended Puerto de la Cruz from pirates. Restored and repurposed as a cultural space with Atlantic views.

iglesia-orotava.desc: The baroque jewel of La Orotava. Two bell towers and blue dome visible from the whole valley. Interior with 18th-century golden altarpieces.

palacio-carta.desc: 18th-century neoclassical palace in central Santa Cruz, now home to Bankinter. Impressive façade and visitable inner courtyard. One of the finest examples of Canarian civil architecture.

museo-bellas-artes.desc: Permanent collection of Canarian painting and sculpture from the 16th century to today. Works by artists like Nicolás Alfaro and Gaspar de Quevedo. Free entry.

catedral-laguna.desc: Cathedral of Our Lady of Remedies, seat of Tenerife's diocese since 1819. Neoclassical facade and neo-Gothic interior, with a magnificent baroque altarpiece dedicated to the Virgin of Remedies. The current church was completed in 1915 over a 16th-century parish. Part of the UNESCO World Heritage ensemble.

casa-lercaro.desc: 16th-century Genoese mansion, home to Tenerife's Museum of History and Anthropology. Built by the Lercaro merchant family, it preserves its Renaissance courtyard, creaking wooden floors and carved galleries. Legend says the ghost of Catalina Lercaro, who took her own life on her wedding day, still walks the halls. 18th-century carriages in a separate room.

museo-ciencia-cosmos.desc: Interactive science and astronomy museum run by the Cabildo and the Canary Astrophysics Institute (IAC). Over 100 interactive modules, planetarium with 6.5 m dome and a real meteorite you can touch. Excellent for families. Tram: line 1, Museo de la Ciencia stop.

museo-militar-almeyda.desc: Located in the 19th-century Fort of Almeyda, between the Almeida ravine and the sea. Home to 'El Tigre', the cannon that severed Nelson's arm during the 1797 attack on Santa Cruz. Uniforms, weapons, historical maps and Guanche objects used in the island's defence. Cartographic research centre.

castillo-san-cristobal.desc: Ruins of Tenerife's first castle (1575), main defence of Santa Cruz bay, hidden beneath Plaza de España. In 1797 Admiral Nelson's attack was repelled from here. Free interpretation centre with wall remains, exhibition on 'El Tigre' cannon and the island's defensive history. The square above was redesigned by Herzog & de Meuron.

convento-san-francisco-garachico.desc: Former 16th-century Franciscan convent (1524), survivor of the 1706 volcano that destroyed Garachico. Now a cultural centre with library, municipal archive and exhibitions. Two cloisters with tea wood, open balconies, stone staircase with Mudejar coffered ceiling. The church keeps its single Latin cross nave. Token entry fee.

iglesia-san-francisco-orotava.desc: Franciscan convent church venerating the Virgin of Charity, brought from Seville in the 17th century. Famous for the 1632 oil miracle, certified by the Church: the lamp lighting the image rekindled by itself and oil began to gush forth, distributed to five thousand people. The miraculous oil is still handed out every 5th of August. Canarian baroque architecture.

mirador-humboldt.desc: ⚠️ The viewpoint building and café remain closed due to licensing issues; the famous photos of the La Orotava Valley can still be taken from the outdoor car park. Historic viewpoint at 320 m above sea level on the TF-21 road between Santa Úrsula and La Orotava. Named after Alexander von Humboldt, who in 1799 knelt before the beauty of the Orotava Valley. Panoramic views of the valley, Puerto de la Cruz, Los Realejos, El Fraile and Las Arenas volcanoes and Mount Teide in the background. Inaugurated in 2010. Café, parking, rest area. Accessible.

mercado-lagunero.desc: Tenerife's most authentic market. Tropical fruits, cheese, mojo, gofio and wrinkled potatoes.

mercado-africano.desc: Santa Cruz's great market. Fresh fish from the dock, tropical fruits and flowers.

bodega-monje.desc: Century-old winery in El Sauzal. D.O. Tacoronte-Acentejo wines with tastings and restaurant.

guachinche-talegazo.desc: One of La Orotava's most recommended guachinches (4.3★, 2,700+ reviews). Grilled meat you cook yourself on a hot stone, outstanding gofio escaldón and house wine. Family-run, rustic, low prices. 📍 Cmo. del Sauce 22 · Daily 1pm-7pm · ☎ +34 643 20 81 01. Booking advised.

guachinche-casa-pedro.desc: One of Tenerife's top-rated guachinches (4.7★, 3,200+ reviews). Homemade Canarian food, outstanding house white wine, warm atmosphere. The goat meat is among the island's finest. 📍 C. La Longuera 10, Los Realejos · 🕐 Fri-Sat 1-5pm & 7-10pm, Mon 1-5pm · ☎ +34 664 78 66 11. Booking essential.

guachinche-ramon.desc: Exceptionally rated guachinche (4.8★, 1,700+ reviews). Hidden gem in La Orotava, totally authentic: looks like a garage but the food is outstanding. Some of the best smoked cheese on the island, smooth homemade red wine, family service. 📍 Cmo. Los Gómez, La Orotava · 🕐 Mon-Thu 11am-7pm, closed Fri-Sun · ☎ +34 686 98 46 02. Arrive early.

guachinche-cubano.desc: One of La Orotava's most famous and oldest guachinches (4.1★, 3,500+ reviews). Maintains classic tradition in decor and cooking. Must-try: ropavieja, carne fiesta, grilled cheese, wrinkled potatoes with mojo and house wine. 📍 Lugar Maestre Juan · 🕐 Wed-Sun (variable hours) · ☎ +34 673 66 02 68. Tends to fill up, booking advised.

guachinche-romance.desc: Highly recommended La Orotava guachinche (4.2★, 2,400+ reviews) with garden and palm trees. Specialities: grilled tomahawk, tableside flambé chorizo, homemade ham croquettes, sautéed mushrooms. House wine and northern views. 📍 Ctra. Gral. Las Cañadas km 9.2, Barroso · 🕐 Wed-Sun (lunch & dinner) · ☎ +34 676 86 96 29.

guachinche-ramal.desc: Wood-fire grill guachinche in La Orotava (4.1★, 1,400+ reviews). Highlights: goat meat, wood-grilled pork ribs, huevos al estampido and homemade desserts (flan). Highly rated house wine. 📍 Ctra. Gral. El Ramal, TF-211 nº17 · 🕐 Wed-Sun · ☎ +34 922 32 13 13.

guachinche-ana-eva.desc: TOP guachinche in La Matanza de Acentejo (4.6★, 8,500+ reviews). Multiple-award winner among Tenerife's best. Exquisite goat meat, grilled chicken, mushrooms with almogrote, gofio escaldón. Fast and very attentive service. 📍 C. Obispo Pérez Cáceres 25 · 🕐 Mon-Fri 1-5pm, closed weekends · ☎ +34 648 93 21 71. Booking essential.

guachinche-bodega-sursula.desc: Top-rated guachinche in Santa Úrsula (4.7★, 370+ reviews). Excellent roasted cheese, Iberian black pork with padrón peppers, wrinkled potatoes, spinach croquettes, homemade mojo. Frequented by locals, great prices. 📍 Ctra. Provincial 28, Santa Úrsula · 🕐 Thu-Sat 1-4pm & 7:30-11pm, Sun-Mon lunch, closed Tue-Wed · ☎ +34 660 59 99 93.

guachinche-guayero.desc: Authentic guachinche in Tegueste (4.5★, 620+ reviews). Traditional Canarian cuisine, lots of meat (pork raised by the owner), excellent papas con mojo. Welcoming local atmosphere, few tourists. 📍 C. Los Pobres 60, Tegueste · 🕐 Wed-Sat 12pm-11pm, Sun 12-6pm, closed Mon-Tue · ☎ +34 822 61 44 32. Couple: ~€40 with wine.

guachinche-cordero.desc: The south's best-known guachinche, set among banana trees (4.2★, 17,500+ reviews). Tables inside a banana plantation (weekends only). Grilled meat, stewed goat meat, house wine. Free bananas with the bill. 📍 TF-652 nº8, Arona · 🕐 Daily 1pm-11pm · ☎ +34 922 73 41 71. Booking strongly advised.

guachinche-el-primero.desc: Famous guachinche-bodegón near Puerto de la Cruz (4.5★, 3,500+ reviews). Outstanding chickpea soup, fish fritters, chicken croquettes and house red wine. Usual queue moves fast. 📍 C. Malpais 10, Santa Úrsula · 🕐 Mon-Sun 12:15-4:45pm, Fri also 7:30-10:15pm · ☎ +34 650 61 02 85. Locals' favourite.

guachinche-casa-lito.desc: Guachinche with panoramic Atlantic terrace (4.1★, 3,500+ reviews). Wood-oven meats: tomahawk, Iberian secreto, roast chicken and churrasco. Gofio escaldón and cheese in honey with a hint of spice. 📍 C. Tijarafe 35 · 🕐 Mon-Tue, Thu 1-5pm, Fri-Sat 1-10pm, Sun 1-5pm, closed Wed · ☎ +34 630 59 00 07.

guachinche-corujera.desc: Rural guachinche 15 min from Puerto de la Cruz (4.1★, 320+ reviews). Abundant home cooking: pork ribs with potatoes and pineapple, smooth red wine. Fast and attentive service. 📍 Ctra. Antigua Corujera 4, Santa Úrsula · 🕐 Mon-Wed and Fri-Sat 1-10:30pm, Sun 1-5:30pm, closed Thu · ☎ +34 922 92 84 65.

guachinche-el-patio.desc: Classic of Tacoronte, the most guachinchero town (4.3★, 1,700+ reviews). Excellent chicken croquettes, grilled cheese, black sausage, cod and freshly baked bread with mojos. 📍 Ctra. Gral. del Norte 191 · 🕐 Mon-Tue and Thu 1-4:30pm, Fri-Sat 1-10:30pm, Sun 1-4:30pm, closed Wed · ☎ +34 600 78 02 27. Outstanding value.

guachinche-basilio.desc: Modern guachinche with sea views (4.4★, 2,700+ reviews). Famous for grilled meat, fried goat cheese, ropa vieja and red wine. Lovely terrace. 📍 C. Obispo Pérez Cáceres 75 · 🕐 Mon and Sun 1-5pm, Tue-Sat 1-11pm · ☎ +34 629 02 84 38.

guachinche-parralito.desc: Authentic guachinche under grapevines (4.4★, 310+ reviews). Traditional cooking: huevos al estampido ("submarine"), carne fiesta, homemade quesillo for dessert. Only open Thu-Sun lunchtime. 📍 C. San Cristóbal 66 · 🕐 Thu-Sun 11:30am-4pm, closed Mon-Wed · ☎ +34 822 09 18 24. Arrive early.

guachinche-casa-yayi.desc: Small, very authentic guachinche in La Matanza. Ropa vieja, salt cod with onions, lentils, chestnuts and good wine. Generous portions at very low prices (~€10/person). 📍 C. San José 10, La Matanza de Acentejo. Real home cooking, family service. Cash recommended.

bodega-insulares.desc: Largest winery of D.O. Tacoronte-Acentejo. Guided tours with tastings, groups many growers together. Produces the well-known Viña Norte and Brumas de Ayosa wines. 📍 Vereda del Medio 48, Tacoronte · 🕐 Mon-Fri 7am-3pm, closed weekends · ☎ +34 922 57 06 17. Booking required.

bodega-el-lomo.desc: Family winery with exceptional rating (4.8★, 145 reviews). Guided tours with tasting of 3 wines (white, rosé, red) and snacks at different spots around the estate. They also make vermouth and vinegar. Excellent views. 📍 C. El Lomo 18, Tegueste · 🕐 Mon-Fri 9:30am-2:30pm, closed weekends · ☎ +34 922 54 52 54. Booking required.

bodega-linaje-pago.desc: Quality wine-tourism winery (4.7★, 82 reviews). Vineyard + cellar tour + tasting of 5 wines with Canarian cheese and cold-cut board (€15/person). Sea and Teide views. 📍 C. Herrera 85, El Sauzal · 🕐 Mon-Fri 9am-2pm (Fri until 5pm), Sat 1-5pm, closed Sun · ☎ +34 640 37 95 64.

bodega-tajinaste.desc: Reference winery in D.O. Valle de La Orotava (4.5★, 123 reviews). Four generations of the family producing award-winning wines. 2h tour with tasting of 6 wines, cold cuts and cheese. 📍 Ctra. TF-212 La Perdoma 4C · 🕐 Tue-Fri 10am-6pm, Sat 10am-2pm, closed Mon and Sun · ☎ +34 622 95 81 57. Booking required.
bodega-tajinaste.cat: Winery · D.O. Valle de La Orotava

bodega-suertes-marques.desc: Internationally recognised among the world's top 100 wineries by Wine & Spirits. Wines from Listán Blanco and Listán Negro grapes from century-old vineyards. Visits by appointment only. 📍 La Perdoma, La Orotava · ☎ +34 922 50 13 00. Iconic labels: Trenzado, La Solana, El Esquilón, Vidonia.
bodega-suertes-marques.cat: Winery · D.O. Valle de La Orotava

bodega-vinatigo.desc: Exceptional winery specialised in native and near-extinct grape varieties (4.8★, 194 reviews). Pioneers in recovering rare grapes like Vijariego, Marmajuelo, Listán Gacho. Tour with tasting of 6 wines. 📍 Trav. Juandana s/n, La Guancha · 🕐 Mon-Fri 8am-4pm, closed weekends · ☎ +34 922 82 87 68. Booking essential.

bodega-cumbres-abona.desc: D.O. Abona cooperative, Spain's highest-altitude D.O. (1,000-1,700 m) (4.5★, 149 reviews). Tenerife's only olive oil producer besides wines. Tasting + tour + shop. 📍 Camino del Viso s/n, Teguedite (Vilaflor) · 🕐 Mon-Fri 7am-3pm, Sat 8am-1pm, closed Sun · ☎ +34 922 76 86 04. Visits by appointment.

gofio-escaldado.desc: Benchmark for traditional Canarian cuisine in Santa Cruz. Wrinkled potatoes, gofio, mojo and fresh fish.

restaurante-drago.desc: 18th-century Canarian house next to the Millennial Dragon Tree, now a restaurant and shop. Canarian cuisine, local cheeses and wines, and a garden terrace among bougainvilleas overlooking the tree.

lago-martianez.desc: Sea water pools complex designed by César Manrique. Iconic architecture and palm trees.

karting.desc: Go-karts for adults and children, mini-golf and attractions in Costa Adeje. Guaranteed fun.

whale-watching.desc: The best whale and dolphin watching in the Atlantic. 300+ resident pilot whales all year round.

teide-teleforico.desc: Ascend to 3,555 m in 8 minutes. Advance booking essential. Views of the entire archipelago.

loro-parque.desc: Europe's best zoo according to TripAdvisor for several consecutive years. Orcas, sea lions, penguins, gorillas, chimpanzees, tigers, sharks (17 m tunnel) and the world's largest parrot collection. Over 50 million visitors since 1972. A must-visit.

aqualand-sur.desc: The largest water park in the Canary Islands. Adrenaline slides, children's area and wave pool. Guaranteed fun for the whole family.

monkey-park.desc: Small refuge zoo founded in 1991 in Arona, specialised in breeding and conservation of endangered primates. Ring-tailed lemurs, squirrel monkeys, gibbons, tortoises, iguanas, crocodiles, big cats and exotic birds. You can feed the animals with food from the park.

forestal-park.desc: The Canary Islands' largest adventure park, at 1,380 m altitude in the protected pine forest of Las Lagunetas (El Rosario), at the gates of Teide National Park. Over 90 treetop games among centuries-old Canary pines: rope bridges, nets, lianas, climbing wall and the longest zip line in the Canaries (230+ m). Colour-coded courses by difficulty (from age 5). Continuous safety line system. Free parking. No phone signal — a real break.

parque-cesar-manrique.desc: César Manrique's posthumous work, opened in 1995, beside the Auditorium and the Palmetum. A 22,000 m² complex with 3 saltwater pools (the main one 6,500 m²), a children's pool with waterfalls, volcanic rock islets, palm trees, restaurants and solarium. Designed with Manrique's signature natural elements. Open every day. September to June 10am-6pm, July and August 10am-7pm. Bus lines 110, 102, 103. Tram: Intercambiador stop.

palmetum.desc: 12-hectare botanical garden dedicated to palms of the world: ~600 species arranged by geographical zones (Madagascar, Caribbean, New Caledonia, Asia, Americas…). Built on a former landfill, opened 2014. Waterfall system, streams, ponds, tropical greenhouse 'Octógono' and viewpoints over Anaga and the ocean. Wheelchair-accessible with lift. Ideal for families: wide paths, café, bird species.

parque-garcia-sanabria.desc: Santa Cruz's largest central urban park (67,230 m²), opened in 1926 and listed as a Cultural Heritage site. Flower clock, fountains, open-air sculptures, tropical and subtropical species, large children's area. Cafés and kiosks. Perfect for a break after the city centre. Free access, open all day.

parque-la-granja.desc: One of Santa Cruz's largest urban parks (built 1969-1976) between the avenues Benito Pérez Armas, Bélgica and Madrid. Royal palms, reed beds, large lawns, children's area renovated in 2023 with accessible facilities, picnic tables, monument to naturalist Félix Rodríguez de la Fuente, amphitheatre, café. The Public Library (House of Culture) and the Espacio La Granja theatre are within the grounds. Free access.

park-la-gesta.desc: The largest children's playground in the Canary Islands (2,500 m²), opened in 2022 next to the Plaza de España in Santa Cruz. Historic theme of the 25th July Gesta: boats, rowing boats, swings, slides, climbing nets, bars, hammocks, 15 m zip line and a telescope. Over 25 inclusive games. Capacity for 480 children. Completely free entry. Rubber flooring for safety.
park-la-gesta.cat: Free Playground · Santa Cruz · Largest in Canary Islands

park-la-vega.desc: La Laguna's most complete park (22,000 m²): children's area with slides and swings, climbing wall, skatepark, basketball courts, table tennis, BMX circuit, pond with water lilies, frogs and turtles, bridges and tree-lined paths. Free and open all year. Ideal for families with children of all ages.
park-la-vega.cat: Free Urban Park · La Laguna · 22,000 m²

park-taoro.desc: Spectacular park on top of Taoro mountain in Puerto de la Cruz, with 100,000 m² of gardens, illuminated waterfalls, paths, viewpoints (Dulce María Loynaz Viewpoint), tropical palms and wild parrots. Children's area with swings, slides and climbing houses in the shade of palm trees. Café with views of Teide. Former Gran Hotel Taoro and Anglican church (1890). Free and permanently open.
park-taoro.cat: Free Park · Puerto de la Cruz · 100,000 m²

park-montillo.desc: One of north Tenerife's best family parks, in La Matanza de Acentejo. 57,000 m² of green space with a central lake, streams and photo-worthy bridges. Facilities: children's playground with slides and swings, skate area, BMX track, sports circuit, amphitheatre, picnic and BBQ areas, café, dog park, interpretation centre with 410 endemic plants (palms, dragon trees, Canarian pines). Wheelchair and pushchair accessible. Free parking. Hours: 7am–10pm daily. Buses 101, 102 and 30 from Santa Cruz/La Laguna. 4.6/5 with 4,200+ Google reviews.
park-montillo.cat: Nature Park · La Matanza de Acentejo · 57,000 m² · Free

minigolf-vivo-americas.desc: Tenerife's top-rated minigolf on TripAdvisor. Pirate theme with 2 x 18-hole courses (Red — easier, Yellow — more challenging). The double ticket lets you play both courses on different days within 7 days. Waterfalls, caves, creative obstacles and Atlantic views. Bar with drinks and snacks, pool tables and arcades. Open every day until midnight. Av. Rafael Puig Lluvina 7, Playa de las Américas. Book online with 5% discount at vivotreasureislandminigolf.com.
minigolf-vivo-americas.cat: Minigolf · 2 x 18 Holes · Las Américas · Pirate Theme

minigolf-kapital-adeje.desc: Seafront minigolf at Puerto Colón (Av. de Colón, Costa Adeje) with spectacular Atlantic views and unique sunsets. Two courses: 12 holes and a new creative, challenging 18-hole course. Deal available for playing both. The owner is especially welcoming. Prize for the winner of each game. Bar with cold Dorada beer and reasonably priced drinks. Hours: 10:30-18:00, closed Saturdays. Walkable from Costa Adeje and Playa de la Pinta.
minigolf-kapital-adeje.cat: Minigolf · Puerto Colón · Costa Adeje · Sea Views

minigolf-wakanda-adeje.desc: Simple, hand-built minigolf in Costa Adeje (Calle Roma, Torviscas–Fañabé area), run by a friendly owner. A quiet, affordable family activity with ocean views nearby. A modest course — some holes may need maintenance — but a fun little activity for a while. Affordable prices. Good for children.

aa-sin-fronteras-adeje.desc: Alcoholics Anonymous group in Adeje (Grupo Sin Fronteras). Meetings Monday and Thursday 19:00-20:30 at the Los Olivos church halls. Free, anonymous and confidential support to stop drinking. Helpline: 629 456 879 (24h).

aa-granadilla-san-isidro.desc: Alcoholics Anonymous group in San Isidro (Granadilla de Abona). Meetings Monday, Wednesday and Friday 19:00-20:30 below the San Isidro Labrador church; open meeting on the last Monday of the month. Free, anonymous support. Tel. 629 456 879 (24h).

aa-harbour-los-cristianos.desc: Alcoholics Anonymous group in Los Cristianos (Arona), Harbour Group. Meetings Monday, Wednesday and Saturday 17:45-18:45 on Avenida Juan Carlos I. Free, anonymous and confidential support. Tel. 613 815 462 / 629 456 879 (24h).

aa-serenidad-realejos.desc: Alcoholics Anonymous Serenidad group in Los Realejos. Meetings Tuesday and Thursday 19:30-21:00 at Calle Chile 4. Free, anonymous and confidential support. Tel. 629 456 879 (24h).

proyecto-hombre-santacruz.desc: Proyecto Hombre Canarias, a leading centre in Tenerife for addiction treatment and prevention (alcohol, drugs and other behaviours). Professional support for individuals and families. Santa Cruz, Pedro Doblado Claverie 34. Mon-Thu 8:00-20:00, Fri 8:00-15:00. Tel. 922 66 10 20.

telefono-esperanza-tenerife.desc: Teléfono de la Esperanza in Tenerife: a free, confidential emotional-support line, available 24 hours, for anyone in crisis, loneliness or distress. Phone and in-person support in Santa Cruz (Av. Ángel Guimerá 35). Tel. 922 33 40 50.

san-miguel-santacruz.desc: Asociación de Cooperación Juvenil San Miguel, an addiction-help and social-support organisation in Tenerife. Support for people with alcohol or other drug problems and their families. Santa Cruz, Calle Sargento Provisional 41. Tel. 922 65 12 51.

san-miguel-laguna.desc: Asociación de Cooperación Juvenil San Miguel, La Laguna branch. Addiction help and social support for people with alcohol or drug problems and their families. Avenida Trinidad 57. Tel. 922 25 58 47.

na-grupo2006-santacruz.desc: Narcotics Anonymous group in Santa Cruz (Grupo 2006). Meetings Tuesday and Thursday 19:30-21:00 at Calle Buenaventura Bonnet 2. Free, anonymous support to stop using drugs. Tel. 605 15 18 03.

cad-icod.desc: Drug Addiction Care Centre (CAD) in Icod de los Vinos. Free public support for people with alcohol or other drug problems and their families. Calle General García Escámez 19, San Marcos. Tel. 922 81 09 62.

parkinson-tf-sede-laguna.desc: Parkinson Tenerife — main office of the Tenerife Parkinson patients' and families' association. Comprehensive support for people with Parkinson and their families: information, psychology, physiotherapy, speech therapy, social work, home care and support groups. Calle San Francisco de Paula 118, Los Baldíos (La Laguna). Tel. 922 62 53 90. parkinsontenerife.org.

parkinson-tf-realejos.desc: Parkinson Tenerife — Integral Care Unit in Los Realejos. Specialised therapies and support for people with Parkinson and their families in northern Tenerife (psychology, physiotherapy, speech therapy, support groups). Calle San Isidro s/n, Los Realejos. Tel. 922 62 53 90.

parkinson-tf-silos.desc: Parkinson Tenerife — Integral Care Unit in Los Silos. Support and therapies for people with Parkinson and their families in the Isla Baja (northwest Tenerife). Plaza de San Bernardo, Los Silos. Tel. 922 62 53 90.

parkinson-tf-granadilla.desc: Parkinson Tenerife — Integral Care Unit in Granadilla de Abona. Support and therapies for people with Parkinson and their families in southern Tenerife (psychology, physiotherapy, speech therapy, support groups). Calle Aguilillas s/n, Granadilla de Abona. Tel. 922 62 53 90.

violencia-sexual-24h-tenerife.desc: Tenerife 24-hour Crisis Centre for victims of sexual violence (Canary Islands Institute for Equality, run by Fundación Ideo). A free, confidential service available 24/7, every day, for women aged 16+ who have suffered sexual violence —recent or past— and for people around them. Psychological, legal and social support. No police report is needed to access. Phone 647 759 126; in an emergency call 112; for information 012. More at caeviolenciasexual.com. For safety, the centre's address is given confidentially when you make contact; this point marks the Institute for Equality.

cavis-violencia-sexual-tenerife.desc: CAVIS — Tenerife's Integral Support Service for Victims of Sexual Violence (Cabildo de Tenerife / Canary Islands Institute for Equality). Free, confidential, specialised in-person support: psychological, legal and social help for women victims of sexual violence and those around them. No report needed. Santa Cruz, Calle Franco de Medina 41 (Edificio HICAN IV). 24h emergencies 647 759 126 or 112; women's helpline 016, 24h.

siam-mujeres-santacruz.desc: SIAM — Integral Support Service for Women (Cabildo de Tenerife). Free, confidential information and psychological, legal and social support for women victims of gender violence. By appointment, at Palacete de Coviella, Calle Francisco de Aguiar y Aguiar 8, Santa Cruz. Emergencies 112; 24h women's helpline 016.

mujer-adeje.desc: Support point for women victims of gender violence in Adeje (Social Services and Equality). Free, confidential information and psychological, legal and social support. Next to the Town Hall, Callejón de los Frailes, Adeje. Tel. 922 75 62 38. Emergencies 112; 24h women's helpline 016.

mujer-san-miguel.desc: Support point for women victims of gender violence in San Miguel de Abona (Social Services and Equality). Free, confidential information and psychological, legal and social support. Next to the Town Hall, Carretera de Los Abrigos 30. Emergencies 112; 24h women's helpline 016.

minigolf-oasis-cristianos.desc: Minigolf in Los Cristianos, the most affordable in south Tenerife (~€4/adult, ~€3/child). Very family-friendly and relaxed. Ideal for a quick game. Quiet atmosphere without crowds. Cash recommended. Near Los Cristianos seafront promenade.

minigolf-parque-santiago.desc: The most distinctive minigolf in Las Américas, at the heart of the Parque Santiago complex (Av. Litoral s/n). 3 courses: 2 x 18-hole and 1 x 9-hole, hand-decorated with coloured ceramic mosaics. Exotic garden with 580 plant species, 60 cactus varieties (some over 80 years old) and a winding stream along the route. Open until midnight. Unlimited playing time. Equipment included. Bar and drinks at the entrance. ~€7/adult, ~€6/child. Cash only.
minigolf-parque-santiago.cat: Minigolf · Las Américas · 3 Courses · Cactus Garden · Until Midnight

minigolf-la-pinta-adeje.desc: 18-hole minigolf in Costa Adeje, next to Playa de La Pinta (C/ Roma 4). With sea views. Price: ~€12 adults, ~€8 children (includes clubs, balls and scorecard). Snack bar on site. Hours: approx 12:00-22:00 (varies). The most challenging of Costa Adeje's minigolf venues.
minigolf-la-pinta-adeje.cat: Minigolf 18 Holes · La Pinta · Costa Adeje · Sea Views

minigolf-precise-resort.desc: 18-hole minigolf course in the subtropical gardens of the Precise Resort in Puerto de la Cruz. Spectacular views of the Atlantic Ocean and Mount Teide. Unique garden setting in north Tenerife. Also accessible to non-hotel guests. Hours: 09:00-00:00. The only public mini golf in north Tenerife.
minigolf-precise-resort.cat: Minigolf 18 Holes · Puerto de la Cruz · North · Teide Views

playa-camison.desc: Calm beach between Las Américas and Los Cristianos. Fine sand and sheltered waters. Very family-friendly.

playa-callao.desc: Dark sand beach with fewer crowds. Peaceful local atmosphere. Beautiful sunsets.

playa-puertito.desc: The main beach of Puertito de Güímar: black sand and pebbles in a cove that calms the swell, with a seafront promenade and parking. Local, family atmosphere, with the nautical club and the hamlet’s restaurants a step away; the Malpaís de Güímar nature reserve frames the horizon. Water shoes recommended for getting in.

playa-puertito-adeje.desc: Small cove of dark sand and pebbles in a fishing hamlet of Adeje, famous for the turtles that used to rest in its bay; sightings are occasional today and they must not be touched or fed. Good snorkelling with plenty of fish. Beach bar by the sand and a coastal path from La Caleta. Very limited parking and major hotel construction works nearby.

roque-bodegas.desc: Wild black sand and gravel beach in Anaga, very close to Benijo. Imposing rock stacks rising from the sea and powerful breaking waves. No services or lifeguard: pure nature.

playa-torviscas.desc: Golden beach continuous with Fañabé in Costa Adeje. Ideal for families with young children, calm waters and full services. Lively atmosphere with seafront promenade.

playa-puerto-santiago.desc: Black volcanic sand beach at the foot of Los Gigantes. Authentic fishing village with local restaurants. Departure point for boat trips to the cliffs.

playa-diego-hernandez.desc: Hidden virgin cove between cliffs in Adeje. Access by 45-minute trail or kayak. Golden sand surrounded by vertical rock walls. One of Tenerife's most beautiful and secret beaches. With a long-standing naturist tradition and a bohemian vibe.

playa-jaquita.desc: Black sand beach in Alcalá, on the west coast, in the municipality of Guía de Isora. It sits right beside the Alcalá Natural Pools, the Charcos La Jaquita, linked to them by the coastal promenade. Free parking next to Hotel Gran Meliá Isora.
playa-jaquita.cat: Black Sand Beach · Alcalá · Guía de Isora

playa-rambla.desc: Hidden beach with natural palm trees and green ravine in Los Realejos. Only accessible on foot via a 20-minute trail through banana plantations. Completely virgin and tourist-free.

playa-amarilla.aviso: Free white-line parking in the residential streets, Aquiles and Poseidón. There is no official car park by the Natural Monument and no paid zone; 5-10 minutes' walk away there is usually space.
playa-amarilla.desc: Volcanic rock beach in yellow and orange tones at the foot of Montaña Amarilla, on the edge of Costa del Silencio. The mountain is a Natural Monument and its headland shelters the bay: the water is usually very calm and clear, and the volcanic seabed makes it one of the best snorkelling spots in the south. ⚠️ It is not sand: it is pebbles and volcanic stone platforms, and you get into the water down ladders fixed to the rock. There is no lifeguard. The area is exposed to the N-NE trade wind and to westerly gusts, although the wind on land does not usually disturb the bay. Free white-line street parking on Calle Aquiles and Calle Poseidón; there is no official car park and no paid zone. Bus stop Minerva (7306) about 700 m away, 8 minutes along the path: lines 470 (Los Cristianos — El Médano) every 30-40 min and 415 (South Airport) hourly.
playa-amarilla.cat: Volcanic Beach · Natural Monument · Costa del Silencio

playa-las-gaviotas.desc: ⚠️ Dogs prohibited by municipal by-law, subject to fines. The busiest nudist beach in the north, next to Teresitas. Black volcanic sand and a very calm and tolerant atmosphere. No services but nearby parking.

hosp-candelaria.desc: Main public reference hospital for southern Tenerife. General and paediatric emergencies 24h.

hosp-huc.desc: Public reference hospital for northern Tenerife. Teaching hospital, all specialties.

hosp-sur.desc: Public hospital in the south. 24h emergency and medical specialties for the region.

hosp-norte.desc: Public hospital serving the north-west region. 24h general emergency.

hosp-hospiten-sur.desc: Reference private hospital in the tourist south. Accepts international insurance.

hosp-quiron-sc.desc: Private hospital in Santa Cruz. 24h emergency, all specialties.

hosp-quiron-adeje.desc: Private hospital in Costa Adeje. Tourist care, multiple languages and international insurers.

hosp-bellevue.desc: Private hospital in Puerto de la Cruz. Specializes in tourist care in the north.
hosp-bellevue.cat: Private Hospital · Puerto de la Cruz

hosp-sjd.desc: Concerted hospital for insurance, accidents and private. Adult emergency 24h.

hosp-parque.desc: Private hospital in central Santa Cruz. 24h adult and paediatric emergency.

hosp-vithas-sct.desc: Private hospital in Santa Cruz with permanent 24h emergency since November 2025. Wide range of specialties: cardiology, neurology, oncology, gynaecology, trauma and more. ICU 24h. Private healthcare reference in the Canary Islands.

hosp-hospiten-rambla.desc: Hospiten private hospital on La Rambla, Santa Cruz. 24h emergency, maternity, paediatrics, surgery and all specialties. Reference centre for tourists in the north of the island.

hosp-uro-tenerife.desc: Specialist urology clinic in Santa Cruz. Island reference for urological conditions.

hosp-ceu-laguna.desc: SCS specialist centre in La Laguna. Specialist consultations, diagnostics, rehabilitation and day hospital. Connected to HUC. Covers La Laguna and northern municipalities.

cs-adeje.desc: Primary care for Adeje. For out-of-hours emergencies, go to hospital.

cs-cristianos.desc: Primary care in Los Cristianos. Out-of-hours emergency at hospital.

cs-pcruz.desc: Medical specialties centre for the Orotava Valley. Tests, X-ray and consultations.

cs-orotava.desc: Health centre with 24h emergency service. Serves the entire La Orotava municipality.

cs-icod.desc: Primary care in Icod. Hospital del Norte nearby for 24h emergencies.

cs-granadilla.desc: Centre with 24h emergency for Granadilla and the south-east area.

cs-guimar.desc: Centre with 24h emergency for Güímar and nearby municipalities.

cs-sanisidro.desc: Primary care in San Isidro. Weekend emergency service.

cs-tacoronte.desc: Centre with 24h emergency for Tacoronte and Acentejo area.

cs-medano.desc: Local clinic in El Médano. Saturday emergency service.

cs-ofra.desc: Urban health centre in Santa Cruz, Ofra-Delicias area.

cs-geneto.desc: Primary care in La Laguna, Geneto area.

cs-arona.desc: SCS Primary Care Centre in Arona town, south Tenerife. Serves Los Cristianos, Las Galletas and Costa del Silencio.

cs-santiago-teide.desc: SCS Primary Care Centre in Santiago del Teide, west Tenerife. Serves Los Gigantes, Puerto de Santiago and Playa de La Arena.
cs-santiago-teide.cat: Health Centre · Santiago del Teide · West

cs-buenavista-norte.desc: SCS medical centre in Buenavista del Norte, northwest Tenerife. Primary care for residents of the island's westernmost municipality. For specialties and emergencies, the reference hospital is Hospital del Norte (Icod de los Vinos).
cs-buenavista-norte.cat: Health Centre · Buenavista del Norte · NW

cs-garachico.desc: SCS clinic in Garachico, on the access road from Icod. Primary care for Garachico and north area residents. Reference hospital: Hospital del Norte de Tenerife (Icod de los Vinos).

farm-salamanca.desc: Large 24h pharmacy in Santa Cruz. Wide selection and nearby parking.

farm-anchieta.desc: Extended-hours pharmacy in La Laguna by Padre Anchieta. On-duty service.

farm-blesa.desc: Busy pharmacy in central Los Cristianos. Good service and competitive prices.

farm-orotava.desc: Pharmacy open 365 days a year, next to Las Dehesas health centre.

farm-anaga.desc: Classic pharmacy on Avenida Anaga, by the port. Professional service.

farm-galletas.desc: Pharmacy in Las Galletas, southern Arona. Authentic coastal village.

farm-pharmadeje.desc: Tourist pharmacy in Costa Adeje. English, German and French. Rotating on-duty service.

farm-hernandez-sct.desc: Permanent 24h duty pharmacy in Santa Cruz de Tenerife. One of the few pharmacies with uninterrupted service in the capital. Essential for night emergencies.

farm-islas-canarias-sct.desc: Pharmacy on Av. Islas Canarias, Santa Cruz. Rotating duty shift. Long weekday hours. Well located in central area.

farm-pozo-pcruz.desc: Pharmacy with long hours in Puerto de la Cruz. Open every day of the year 9am–10pm, including public holidays. One of the most accessible for tourists in the north of the island.

farm-bethencourt-pcruz.desc: Pharmacy with extended hours in Puerto de la Cruz. Open 365 days a year 8:30am–10pm. Rotating night duty. Well located in tourist area.

farm-americas-arona.desc: Pharmacy in Los Cristianos, tourist south zone. Long hours and service in several languages. Rotating duty with other pharmacies in the area.

farm-adeje-austria.desc: Pharmacy in Adeje centre. Long weekday hours. Rotating duty with other pharmacies in Adeje and Costa Adeje area.

gas-tf1-granadilla.desc: Repsol petrol station by TF-1 in Granadilla. Shop and car wash. Easy motorway access.

gas-tf1-guaza.desc: BP petrol station in Guaza, Arona exit. Good stop before Los Cristianos and Las Américas.

gas-tf1-guaza2.desc: Cepsa station at the Los Cristianos exit off TF-1. Always busy, always open.

gas-tf1-adeje.desc: Repsol by Costa Adeje. High-traffic tourist area. Large service area with shop.

gas-tf1-candelaria.desc: Cepsa station at the Candelaria exit. Strategic point between north and south. Full service.

gas-tf1-guimar.desc: BP at the Güímar exit. Near the Pyramids of Güímar. Good facilities.

gas-tf5-lalaguna.desc: Repsol at La Laguna exit on TF-5. One of the busiest in the north. Automatic car wash.

gas-tf5-tacoronte.desc: Cepsa by the Tacoronte exit. Wine and guachinche area. Coffee and shop available.

gas-tf5-ptocz.desc: BP at the motorway entrance to Puerto de la Cruz. Very practical for tourists. Spacious and well-lit.

gas-tf5-icod.desc: Repsol in Icod, very close to the Millennial Dragon Tree. Refuelling point in the north-west of the island.

gas-tf2-lalaguna.desc: Cepsa on TF-2, La Laguna exit heading south. Key point between the airport and the capital.

gas-tf2-aeropuerto.desc: BP next to Reina Sofía Airport (TFS). Essential for returning hire cars with a full tank.

gas-tf1-abades.desc: Petrol station on TF-1 km 44, Abades/Arico area. Important stop on the southern motorway eastern section. One of few stations between the airport and Güímar.

gas-tf82-los-gigantes.desc: DISA on the descent to Los Gigantes, TF-82/Puerto Santiago km 1.5. West zone. Essential before continuing north along the west coast or up to Santiago del Teide.

gas-tf21-aguamansa.desc: ⚠️ LAST petrol station before Teide National Park going up TF-21 from La Orotava (Aguamansa). NO petrol stations in the National Park. Essential to fill up here before going up to Teide.

gas-tf5-el-bohio.desc: DISA on TF-5 km 25, La Matanza de Acentejo. Northern motorway, well located between La Laguna and Puerto de la Cruz.

gas-tf5-el-sauzal.desc: Repsol on TF-5 km 22.5, El Sauzal. Northern area between La Laguna and Tacoronte. One of the easiest petrol stations to reach from the northern motorway.

gas-tf51-vilaflor.desc: Petrol station on the TF-51 Arona-Vilaflor at km 4. Southern inland. Important for anyone heading up to Vilaflor (Spain's highest village) or reaching the National Park from the south. The last petrol station before the high ground.

gas-tf82-guia-isora.desc: Shell on TF-82, Guía de Isora km 120. Southwest Tenerife. Important stop between Adeje and Los Gigantes.
gas-tf82-guia-isora.cat: Petrol Station · TF-82 · Guía de Isora

gas-tf5-los-realejos.desc: DISA on TF-5 km 46, Los Realejos. North between Puerto de la Cruz and Icod de los Vinos. Useful for those continuing to Garachico or northwest.

puerto-santa-cruz.desc: ⚠️ Restricted access commercial port. The largest port in the Canary Islands and one of the most important in the Atlantic. Container, cruise and cargo berths. Great ocean liners dock here — spectacular from the Maritime Park. Only accessible to professionals and cruise passengers with documentation. The exterior promenade IS public.

puerto-los-cristianos.desc: Mixed port: commercial (ferries) and fishing. Fred Olsen and Naviera Armas ferries to La Gomera, La Palma and El Hierro depart from here. Embarkation area with controlled access for ticketed passengers. The restaurant area and exterior promenade ARE public and very lively. Starting point for boat excursions to the south.

puerto-colon-adeje.desc: Tenerife's most touristic marina. Over 300 berths in the heart of Costa Adeje. Departure point for all southern sea excursions: whale watching, catamarans, tourist submarines, jet skis, sport fishing. Restaurants, shops and very lively atmosphere all day. Fully accessible to the public.

marina-santa-cruz.desc: Modern sports marina in Santa Cruz next to the César Manrique Maritime Park. Leisure berths with full services. Seafront promenade with bars and restaurants with ocean views. Very close to the Tenerife Auditorium. The promenade and restaurant area are fully public.

puerto-gigantes.desc: One of the most spectacular marinas in the Canary Islands, nestled at the foot of the Los Gigantes cliffs (600m). Departure point for whale and dolphin watching, diving and snorkelling excursions. Restaurants with unique cliff views. Very busy in summer. Fully accessible to the public.

puerto-radazul.desc: Quiet sports marina in Radazul urbanisation, east coast of Tenerife. Local and family atmosphere, less touristy than those in the south. Good nautical services for leisure craft. Nautical club with restaurant and terrace with sea views. Ideal for a quiet meal by the Atlantic.

marina-sur-galletas.desc: Marina opened in 2009 in Las Galletas, a village with a great fishing tradition in the south. Quiet and well-equipped marina with multiple nautical services. Restaurants with authentic maritime atmosphere. Sport fishing and sea excursions. More authentic and less crowded than Puerto Colón.

puerto-guimar.desc: Coastal bathing village of Puertito de Güímar, east coast, with a small nautical club. Official dog beach adjacent. Solarium and swimming area by the entrance. Authentic local atmosphere very different from the mass tourism in the south. Calm waters protected by breakwaters.

puerto-garachico.desc: Historic port in Garachico, the most beautiful village in the north. It was Tenerife's largest port until the 1706 volcanic eruption buried it under lava. The current port is small and picturesque, surrounded by the famous El Caletón volcanic natural pools. Unique historic atmosphere. Not suitable for large vessels.

puerto-candelaria.desc: La Galera marina in Candelaria, municipality of the Patron of the Canary Islands. Nautical facilities next to the Basilica of the Virgin of Candelaria. Quiet local atmosphere. Good stopping point on the east coast between Santa Cruz and Güímar.

puerto-pcruz-nautico.desc: Historic nautical club in Puerto de la Cruz with sports and nautical facilities. Traditional fishing dock with authentic maritime atmosphere. Fresh fish restaurants area. Puerto de la Cruz fishing port is one of the most picturesque in the north of the island.
puerto-pcruz-nautico.cat: Fishing & Nautical Port · Puerto de la Cruz

puerto-playa-san-juan.desc: Fishing and sports port in Playa San Juan, one of the most peaceful villages in the southwest. Very authentic with traditional fishing boats. Fresh fish restaurants direct from the sea. Views of La Gomera on clear days. Far from mass tourism — an authentic Canarian corner.

puerto-amarilla-marina.desc: Modern marina 10 min from Tenerife South airport. 350 berths next to Amarilla Golf — hole 12 overlooks the sea in a unique image with Teide in the background. Tourist submarine excursions, diving and snorkelling. Ocean-view restaurants.

puerto-rcnt-santa-cruz.desc: Tenerife's most important nautical club, founded in 1902. Over 4,500 members. Complete sports facilities: sailing, tennis, swimming. Leisure berths. Elegant social atmosphere. Reference for nautical sport in the Canary Islands. Port entrance IS public for restaurant and events.

puerto-marina-tenerife-sc.desc: Sports marina in the Santa Cruz Fishing Dock, managed by the Port Authority. Nautical facilities with leisure berths. Authentic maritime atmosphere next to Puerto Chico. Good option for boats visiting the capital.

puertito-alcala.desc: Small and authentic fishing port in Alcalá, Guía de Isora municipality. Traditional fishing boats and peaceful maritime village atmosphere. Fresh fish restaurants by the sea. Far from mass tourism, a gem for those seeking authentic Tenerife. Ideal for sunset.
