puertito-los-abrigos.desc: Traditional fishing port in Los Abrigos, one of the most genuine villages in the south. Fish market opened in 2013. Promenade restaurants serve freshly caught fish — one of the best places in Tenerife for fresh fish. Maritime atmosphere without tourist artifice.

puertito-tajao.desc: Small fishing village in San Miguel de Tajao, southeast coast. Active fishermen's guild. Authentic maritime village with traditional boats. Diving and snorkelling area. Sea-view restaurants with excellent daily catch. Relatively unknown to tourists — hidden gem of the southeast.

puertito-poris-abona.desc: Small pier in Porís de Abona, southeast coast. Traditional artisan fishing fleet. El Porís and El Bonito beaches adjacent. Authentic Canarian village atmosphere away from tourism. Good starting point for coastal hiking routes in the southeast.

puertito-san-marcos.desc: Small fishing and tourist port in San Marcos, coastal district of Icod de los Vinos. Very popular dark volcanic sand beach with families. Fresh fish restaurants along the seafront. Authentic local atmosphere with ocean views from the north. Only 10 min from the Millennial Drago Tree.

puertito-el-medano.desc: ⚠️ There is no marina: boats and windsurf schools anchor in the open bay off the beach. Open bay of El Médano, Tenerife's windsurfing and kitesurfing capital. Home to international competitions. El Médano promenade is one of the liveliest in the south. Young active atmosphere, very different from south coastal tourism.

puertito-la-caleta.desc: ⚠️ There is no port or dock: this is the bathing and restaurant seafront of the village of La Caleta. Small fishing village in La Caleta, between Costa Adeje and Playa San Juan. Authentic and peaceful just a few km from the tourist area. Fish restaurants straight from the fish market. Start of the Costa Adeje promenade. Traditional boats and local atmosphere contrasting with mass tourism.

puertito-san-andres-norte.desc: ⚠️ There is no separate harbour: this is the village seafront. The nearest dock is the Dársena Pesquera in Santa Cruz. Seafront of the fishing village of San Andrés, next to the famous Las Teresitas beach. Active fishermen's guild. Authentic maritime atmosphere 8 km from Santa Cruz. Fish and seafood restaurants by the sea. Can be combined with a visit to Las Teresitas. Historic area north of Santa Cruz.

puerto-chico-sct.desc: Small sports marina next to Marina Tenerife in the Santa Cruz Fishing Dock. Nautical facilities managed by the Port Authority. Good views of Santa Cruz Port and Teide on clear days. Quiet and authentic maritime atmosphere.

puerto-mesa-del-mar.desc: ⚠️ There is no port or dock: a residential coastal area with natural pools and a beach. Coastal enclave of Mesa del Mar, Tacoronte, north Tenerife. Small and family-friendly, next to the volcanic natural pools of Mesa del Mar. Authentic local atmosphere. Good views of the north Atlantic. Recreational fishing area. Relatively quiet, off the main tourist routes.
puerto-mesa-del-mar.cat: Sports Marina · Mesa del Mar · Tacoronte

puerto-el-pris.desc: Small fishing port in El Pris, Tacoronte. Much appreciated by locals for swimming in its natural pools and fishing. Northern fishing village atmosphere without mass tourism. Good views of Mesa del Mar. Diving and snorkelling area in calm waters.

puerto-granadilla-comercial.desc: ⚠️ Completely restricted access commercial port. Newly built industrial port in Granadilla de Abona, south Tenerife. Bulk cargo, container and special goods berths. No public access — port industrial zone. Under Port Authority of Santa Cruz de Tenerife administration.

puertito-fasnia.desc: ⚠️ No port facilities: a small rocky cove with minimal natural shelter and beached boats. Small fishing port in Fasnia, municipality on the southeast coast. Traditional fishing boats in a quiet cove. Authentic Canarian village atmosphere far from mass tourism. Nearby volcanic natural pools are popular with locals. Area of great natural beauty with little visitor traffic.

puertito-la-jaca.desc: Small pier in La Jaca, hamlet of San Miguel de Abona, southeast coast. Traditional fishing area. La Jaca beach adjacent. Solitary and natural setting much appreciated by those seeking unspoilt corners. Good viewpoint for the unspoilt southeast coast.

puertito-los-silos.desc: ⚠️ There is no harbour or dock here: a stony cove with a seafront promenade by the whale skeleton. Boats operate from Garachico. Coastal corner of Los Silos, northwest Tenerife. Quiet fishing village next to Teno Rural Park. Traditional fishing boats. Maritime square with fresh fish restaurants. Snorkelling area in crystal clear waters. One of the most peaceful and authentic localities in the northwest.

buceo-los-gigantes.desc: Los Gigantes is one of Tenerife's best diving destinations, with Europe's highest sea cliffs (600m) as underwater backdrop. Los Gigantes Diving Centre, at berth 6 of the Marina, has guided PADI dives to top sites for decades: La Corona cave, volcanic reefs, green turtles and rays. Average visibility 20-30m. Water temperature 18-24°C year-round. Open Water courses from scratch. Also snorkelling and discovery dives. Daily boat departures. Open Mon-Sat 9:30-16:00.
buceo-los-gigantes.cat: Diving & Snorkel · Los Gigantes · PADI · Cliffs

buceo-los-cristianos.desc: Los Cristianos has several PADI dive centres on the Paseo Marítimo, next to the harbour. The best-known is Club de Buceo Rincón de Arona (between Playa Las Vistas and Playa Los Cristianos), with its own 12-diver boat. Dives go to El Pequeño Puerto, Abades reef, La Caleta and the El Condesito wreck. Green turtles, manta rays, schools of tropical fish. Average visibility 20-25m. Temperature 18-24°C. PADI courses, discovery dives, snorkelling. Morning and afternoon departures. WhatsApp bookings.
buceo-los-cristianos.cat: Diving & Snorkel · Los Cristianos · South · PADI

buceo-puerto-colon.desc: Puerto Colón in Costa Adeje is the most important water sports hub in south Tenerife. Scuba Point (PADI 5 Star IDC, C/ Puerto Colón 130) is one of the island's most recognised dive centres, active since 1999. Guided dives to La Caleta, Los Morteros (nature reserve), El Puertito de Adeje (free-swimming turtles), caves and volcanic reefs. Boat snorkelling, Open Water, Advanced and Rescue courses. Divemaster school. Daily departures 9:30 and 14:00. The only dive boat in Tenerife with an on-board toilet.
buceo-puerto-colon.cat: Diving & Snorkel · Puerto Colón · PADI 5★ IDC · Costa Adeje

buceo-puerto-cruz.desc: Atlantik Dive Centre (PADI 5 Star Gold Palm IDC) has operated since 1994 in Puerto de la Cruz, north Tenerife. Their boat Gitano takes divers to the north's best underwater sites: La Catedral (volcanic arch at 30m, groupers, morays, parrotfish), El Garachico Tunnel (iconic volcanic tunnel at 13m), Rapadura, Cueva de la Matanza, Baja Realejos and Chimenea. Average visibility 20-25m. Temperature 18-22°C. Unique volcanic seabeds: walls, caves, basalt arches. PADI courses from Open Water to instructor. Discovery dives from age 10. Also snorkelling trips.
buceo-puerto-cruz.cat: Diving & Snorkel · Puerto de la Cruz · North · PADI 5★

buceo-las-galletas.desc: Las Galletas in south Tenerife is one of the island's most active diving hubs. The Punta Rasca and El Faro area offers volcanic rocky seabeds to 50 metres depth with extraordinary marine diversity: rays, groupers, sea bream, barracudas, the very rare frogfish (perfectly camouflaged), puffer fish, black coral and numerous arches and caves. All levels. Expert divers can reach -50m on rocky drop-offs. El Bufadero, near Los Cristianos (10m depth), is an easy dive for all levels with turtles and eagle rays. Reference centre: Dive Tenerife Las Galletas.
buceo-las-galletas.cat: Diving & Snorkel · Las Galletas · South · Punta Rasca · El Faro

buceo-tabaiba.desc: Tabaiba Baja, northeast of Santa Cruz, is home to Tenerife's most accessible wreck dive. El Peñón is a 35-metre tugboat intentionally sunk in 2006 to create an artificial reef on a sandy seabed at 10-18 metres. Easy shore access. The interior can be explored: engine room, forward cabin. Outside: dense schools of barracuda, sea bream, horse mackerel, sardines, trumpetfish and parrotfish. Also rays and large amberjacks in open water around the wreck. Level: intermediate. Shore dive, no boat needed.
buceo-tabaiba.cat: Diving · El Peñón Wreck · Tabaiba · Santa Cruz · Intermediate

kayak-los-gigantes.desc: Kayaking beneath the highest sea cliffs in Europe is Tenerife's most iconic water experience. From Los Gigantes Harbour you paddle alongside volcanic walls up to 600 metres high that drop vertically into the sea. The standard route goes to Barranco Seco, with a stop to swim in coves inaccessible by land. Bottlenose dolphins, pilot whales and turtles can be spotted in season. Reference company: Teno Activo. Departures every day of the year. No previous experience needed — basic briefing at the harbour before setting off. Duration: ~2 hours. Single and double kayaks.
kayak-los-gigantes.cat: Kayak · Los Gigantes · 600m Cliffs · All Year

kayak-la-caleta.desc: La Caleta de Adeje is south Tenerife's most popular kayak starting point. From this small fishing village, kayak takes you to three completely hidden coves inaccessible by land: Playa de Los Morteros (rocky reef, 20 min), Playa Hernández (white sand, snorkelling) and El Puertito de Adeje (1h — 'Turtle Bay', where several green turtles live in the wild). Reference company: Surf Life Tenerife (fish farm visit included on some tours). Very calm waters, ideal for beginners and families. Single and double kayaks.
kayak-la-caleta.cat: Kayak · La Caleta · Hidden Coves · Turtles · South

kayak-los-cristianos.desc: Los Cristianos is one of the south's best kayak spots for beginners. Kayak + snorkelling tours of around 2.5 hours depart from the harbour to Cueva del Palmar and the Playa Las Vistas Marine Reserve. Sea turtles are frequently spotted. Reference company: Kayak Academy Tenerife (daily departures). Dolphins also possible. Protected waters. Single and double kayaks available. Ideal for families.
kayak-los-cristianos.cat: Kayak · Los Cristianos · South · Turtles · Beginners

kayak-radazul.desc: Radazul, a small marina south of Santa Cruz, is the most recognised transparent kayak hub in northeast Tenerife. Glass-bottomed kayaks allow you to see the volcanic seabed while paddling. Dark, calm volcanic sand waters with great marine biodiversity: tropical fish, octopus, rays, starfish. Very popular with locals. Easy access from Santa Cruz (15 min). Reference company: Radazul Paddle & Kayak. Suitable for all levels. Also SUP (Stand Up Paddleboard).
kayak-radazul.cat: Transparent Kayak · Radazul · Santa Cruz · SUP

kayak-punta-teno.desc: Punta de Teno, at the far northwest tip of Tenerife within Teno Rural Park, offers the island's most wild and unexplored kayak route. Crystal clear water, spectacular volcanic formations, absolute silence and direct views of La Gomera and the Los Gigantes cliffs in the distance. No crowds. Starting point from Punta de Teno itself (access only by shuttle bus TF-369 from Buenavista, or bicycle — cars restricted). Advanced route due to variable north Atlantic conditions. Good weather and experienced guide only.
kayak-punta-teno.cat: Kayak · Punta de Teno · Teno Rural Park · Advanced

escal-arico.desc: The Arico Massif is the most important climbing area in Tenerife and one of the international references for bouldering in Europe. The Arico Nuevo gorge concentrates over 240 water-polished volcanic basalt boulders in an open canyon. Ideal October-April (cloudy or cool). Beyond bouldering, there is sport climbing (multiple sectors: El Río, Las Vegas, El Patio) with routes from 4 to 8c. Erik Vaquero's Red Guide (2022) describes 1,300+ routes across 17 sectors across the island. Tenerife Climbing House (C/La Asomadita 8, Arico) is the reference hostel and climbing school for international climbers. Access: from Arico Nuevo, descend via C/ Las Cuevas towards the gorge.

escal-guaria.desc: Guaría in Guía de Isora municipality is one of south Tenerife's most popular sport climbing sectors. Volcanic basalt wall with mid-to-high difficulty routes (5c-8a). Dry and sunny climate almost year-round — ideal when Arico is too hot. Requires access permit (can be obtained via QR code on site). Atlantic and La Gomera views from the upper routes. Car access from TF-82 road.
escal-guaria.cat: Climbing · Guaría · Guía de Isora · South · Sport

escal-canada-capricho.desc: Cañada del Capricho in Teide National Park (2,000m altitude) is Tenerife's high-mountain climbing paradise. Angular volcanic basalt towers, walls and pinnacles in a unique high-mountain setting. Routes from 6a upwards with real exposure. Roque Cinchado and nearby formations offer multi-pitch climbing with Teide and Las Cañadas views. Cool temperatures year-round — ideal in summer when the south is very hot. TF-21 access. Some sectors require National Park permit.
escal-canada-capricho.cat: Climbing · Teide · High Mountain · Sport · National Park

escal-anaga.desc: Anaga Rural Park concentrates Tenerife's longest traditional and multi-pitch climbing routes — around 100 in total. Roque Negro and Roque de Las Ánimas are the most iconic formations. Climbing on water-polished volcanic rock with spectacular views of the Atlantic and laurisilva forests. Experienced trad and multi-pitch climbers only. Routes require self-protection skills. Wild, lightly visited atmosphere. Difficult access via forest tracks.

pesca-deportiva-puerto-colon.desc: Puerto Colón is the main sport fishing hub in south Tenerife. Fishing charters leave daily from its docks in search of the Atlantic's great pelagic species: blue marlin (up to 500 kg), white marlin, bluefin tuna, skipjack tuna, wahoo, swordfish and dorado. All fishing is catch-and-release. The La Gomera strait has the highest density of blue marlin in European waters. Best season: May-November. 25-35ft boats with certified skippers. Equipment included. Advance booking recommended.
pesca-deportiva-puerto-colon.cat: Sport Fishing · Puerto Colón · Marlin · Tuna · South

pesca-deportiva-los-cristianos.desc: Los Cristianos harbour is south Tenerife's second sport fishing hub, with several active charters for blue marlin, yellowfin tuna, wahoo and barracuda. Less frequent departures than Puerto Colón, but more relaxed and authentic. Also artisanal coastal fishing charters: sea bream, vieja (Canarian parrotfish), octopus and dorado. Average price: €50-80/person for shared trips. Private boats also available. Season: year-round for coastal; May-November for pelagics.
pesca-deportiva-los-cristianos.cat: Sport Fishing · Los Cristianos · South · Marlin · Artisanal

pesca-los-gigantes.desc: Los Gigantes Harbour has a long tradition of deep-sea sport fishing. The Nashira Uno charter has operated from this port for over 30 years and has won the only two championships held there. Daily departures trolling between the Los Gigantes cliffs and the La Gomera strait. Techniques: deep-sea trolling (blue marlin, white marlin, bigeye tuna, yellowfin tuna, dorado, wahoo, wahoo, swordfish) and bottom fishing (sea bream, grouper). Also coastal artisanal fishing. Departure times: 09:30 (4h or 7h) and 13:30 (3h). Private or shared charter.
pesca-los-gigantes.cat: Sport Fishing · Los Gigantes · Marlin · 30+ years · West

pesca-los-abrigos.desc: Los Abrigos is an authentic, quiet fishing village in south Tenerife (Granadilla de Abona municipality), known for its fresh seafood restaurants. The small harbour hosts artisanal fishing boats and some sport fishing charters for coastal species: sea bream, sama, vieja (Canarian parrotfish), grouper, barracuda, black bream. Also light trolling for small pelagics (bonito, skipjack, mackerel, dorado). 100% local atmosphere. No mass tourism. The fishermen's cooperative is one of the most active in the south.
pesca-los-abrigos.cat: Sport Fishing · Los Abrigos · South · Artisanal · Seafood

deporte-garcia-sanabria.desc: The largest urban park in central Santa Cruz (67,230 m²) includes an outdoor fitness area with municipal calisthenics equipment, a running track, and plenty of open space for sport. Completely free. Open access all day. Very popular with locals for morning running and daily exercise.

deporte-parque-granja.desc: Large urban park in Santa Cruz with a well-defined running circuit among palm trees and green areas. Calisthenics zone with bars and parallel bars installed by the Town Hall. Amphitheatre and open spaces for group exercises. Free and open access. Very popular with local athletes at dawn and dusk.

deporte-rambla-sc.desc: Santa Cruz's most emblematic running boulevard: 2.5 km of tree-lined avenue with a dedicated lane for runners, cyclists and pedestrians. Lined with sculptures and gardens. Free and accessible all day. One of the most pleasant urban exercise routes in the Canary Islands, even in summer thanks to tree shade.

deporte-medano-playa.desc: El Médano beach offers unique free sports facilities in Tenerife: beach volleyball courts, beach football area, basketball hoops and calisthenics space next to the promenade. Tenerife's windsurfing and kitesurfing capital. The promenade is one of the liveliest in the south, with a young and sporty atmosphere. All outdoor and free.

deporte-costa-adeje-paseo.desc: Costa Adeje seafront promenade has outdoor calisthenics and fitness zones between Playa del Duque and Playa Fañabé. Pull-up bars, parallel bars, low bars and outdoor weight machines installed by Adeje Council. Free and open 24h. Sea views while exercising. Very popular with both tourists and residents.

deporte-los-cristianos-paseo.desc: Los Cristianos seafront promenade includes an outdoor calisthenics zone with pull-up bars, dip bars and street workout equipment installed next to the beach. Direct sea and harbour views. Completely free. Available 24h. Very busy early morning and at sunset. The beach setting makes it one of the best-atmosphere outdoor gyms in Tenerife.

deporte-puerto-cruz-piscina.desc: Puerto de la Cruz has a running and outdoor fitness zone along its coastal promenade next to Lago Martiánez pools. Free outdoor exercise space with Atlantic views. Puerto de la Cruz coastal promenade is one of the most beautiful in the north for sport at dawn. Calisthenics bars in the coastal park.
deporte-puerto-cruz-piscina.cat: Running · Calisthenics · Puerto de la Cruz

deporte-orotava-parque.desc: La Orotava has free outdoor sports areas at various points in the municipality: futsal and basketball courts in Parque del Ranilla, calisthenics bars in the municipal park and free training space. Free access. The municipality invests in public sports facilities for residents and visitors.

deporte-san-isidro-zona.desc: San Isidro (Granadilla de Abona) has a free public sports area with outdoor futsal courts and a calisthenics zone in the municipal park. Very popular with local residents. Quiet authentic southern area away from mass tourism. Family and neighbourhood atmosphere. Free access all day.

deporte-laguna-parque-avenidas.desc: La Laguna municipality, a UNESCO World Heritage city, has outdoor fitness and calisthenics zones at Parque Las Avenidas and nearby areas. Free municipal facilities with bars, outdoor exercise machines and space for functional training. Very popular with ULL university students. Free access all day.

deporte-candelaria-paseo.desc: Candelaria seafront promenade includes an outdoor calisthenics zone and a running lane by the sea with views of the Basilica of the Virgin of Candelaria. Bars installed by the council. Completely free. The setting is spectacular: black volcanic sand, Guanche statues and the Atlantic Ocean. Ideal for a sport session with history and scenery.

deporte-palm-mar-fitness.desc: Palm-Mar, a small coastal village in the south, has a municipal outdoor fitness area and publicly accessible padel and tennis courts. Quiet and very local environment. One of the few areas in the south where you can train for free with sea views outside tourist circuits. Ideal for athletes seeking peace.

deporte-guia-isora-skate.desc: Guía de Isora has a free municipal skatepark and multi-sport court (futsal, basketball) at the municipality's sports facilities. Free access to outdoor courts. Quiet local atmosphere. A gem for skaters and athletes in the southwest, a little-touristy area with well-maintained council facilities.

deporte-arona-multideporte.desc: The Cabildo of Tenerife has installed three free, open-access multi-sport courts in Arona (2025 Insular Sports Infrastructure Plan): next to Las Américas Golf, in El Fraile and in La Estrella Urbanisation (Las Rosas). 30×15 m courts approved for basketball, volleyball, handball and futsal. No booking required. Managed by Arona council.

deporte-realejos-street-workout.desc: Calisthenics and street workout park in Parque Juan Marrero, La Montaña district (Los Realejos). Certified by the World Street Workout and Calisthenics Federation (WSWCF). Funded 80% by the Cabildo de Tenerife and 20% by the council. Completely free and outdoor. Los Realejos also has parks in El Nazareno and Parque Juan Carlos I (near the schools and Municipal Market). Open 24 hours.

deporte-sc-tenerife-barmania.desc: Barmanía Park calisthenics park in Santa Cruz de Tenerife, one of the most highly rated in the capital (4.4/5 with over 48 reviews). Spacious and green with natural shade. Pull-up bars, parallel bars and street workout equipment. Water fountain nearby. Meeting point for group training. Intermediate level. Free and outdoor. Very popular with Tenerife's local calisthenics community.

deporte-sc-chimisay.desc: Calisthenics park in the Chimisay neighbourhood, Santa Cruz (C/ Eladio Afonso y González 4, 38010). Good condition pull-up bars, with a nearby fountain. Neighbourhood atmosphere, very popular with local residents. Free access. Intermediate level. Santa Cruz calisthenics parks have rubber surfaces to cushion falls and are open all day.

deporte-sc-plaza-espana.desc: Calisthenics park next to the Plaza de España Tunnel in central Santa Cruz (rated 4.7/5). Spacious area in a central urban location, with shade. Bars in good condition though with some wear. Regular meeting point for street workout groups. Very well located to access from any part of the capital. Free and open all day.

deporte-skatepark-granja-sc.desc: 2,500 m² skatepark inside Parque La Granja, Santa Cruz, designed by architect and skater Daniel Yábar. The design incorporates Tenerife's landscape diversity: organic concrete shapes in brown and ochre tones, with basalt rocks as natural obstacles. Central mini ramp, various quarters, ramps, street section with steps, rails and hubbas of different heights, boxes and flat ground rails. Free access within the park.

deporte-skatepark-laguna-copernico.desc: Modern skatepark in La Manzanilla neighbourhood, La Laguna (C/ Copérnico, CP 38208). Opened over 20 years ago and recently renovated and modernised: wings and edges updated with skate-specific materials, two steps and an additional ramp built, a central pyramid added and general paintwork refreshed. Features banks and rails, hips, rollin and other obstacles. Free.

deporte-pista-multideporte-cabildo-reale.desc: Free-access multi-sport court installed in Los Realejos by the Cabildo de Tenerife's Insular Sports Infrastructure Plan (one of 25 installed across the island). 30×15 m court approved for basketball, volleyball, handball, futsal and badminton. No advance booking, free use for all ages. Municipal management. Los Realejos was among the first municipalities to receive these facilities under the 'Tenerife Saludable' programme.

deporte-pista-multideporte-icod.desc: Free-access multi-sport court delivered to Icod de los Vinos council by the Cabildo de Tenerife in 2024, as part of the Insular Sports Infrastructure Plan. Approved 30×15 m court for basketball, volleyball, handball, futsal and tennis. Free access, no booking required, for all ages. Located in a neighbourhood area, ideal for daily sport in the Drago Milenario municipality.

deporte-pista-multideporte-tacoronte.desc: Free-access multi-sport court in Tacoronte, installed by the Cabildo de Tenerife in 2024 as part of the Insular Sports Infrastructure Plan ('Tenerife Saludable'). Approved for basketball, volleyball, handball, futsal and badminton. Free use without booking, for all ages. Tacoronte is a wine-producing municipality in the north, known for its DO Tacoronte-Acentejo wines. This court adds to the municipality's sports facilities.

deporte-valle-san-lorenzo-kenguru.desc: Kenguru Pro calisthenics park in Valle San Lorenzo, Arona municipality (CP 38626), rated 4.6/5 by over 34 users. Well equipped for outdoor training, relaxed atmosphere with shade. Nearby water fountain. Intermediate level. Regular meeting point for the south island street workout community. Free and open all day.
deporte-valle-san-lorenzo-kenguru.cat: Calisthenics Kenguru Pro · Valle San Lorenzo

bici-bc1-inicio.desc: Start of official BC-1 cycling route, Tenerife's longest (84.8 km). Begins at La Esperanza, crossing the north from east to west through laurel forest, pine forests and the Teno massif. Orange waymarked by Cabildo. IBP index: 120 (high). Experienced cyclists only. Helmet required.
bici-bc1-inicio.cat: Official MTB BC-1 · La Esperanza · Cabildo

bici-bc2-inicio.desc: Official Cabildo BC-2 cycling route: the most accessible in the network. Short, moderate elevation, orange waymarked in the Corona Forestal. Ideal for beginners and families. Canarian pines with Teide views. Helmet recommended.

bici-bc5-vilaflor.desc: Official BC-5 route in Vilaflor pine forests, Corona Forestal. 15.7 km, 430 m elevation — moderate level. Vilaflor is one of Spain's highest villages (1,400 m). Canarian pines with south-facing views. Duration: ~1h40. Orange waymarked.

bici-teide-subida.desc: One of Europe's most spectacular cycling climbs. TF-21 from La Orotava (350 m) to Teide (2,100 m): 50 km, 1,700+ m elevation. Well-maintained tarmac. Scenery shifts from laurel forest to pines and lunar volcano. Best at dawn. For fit cyclists only.

bici-anaga-cruz-carmen.desc: Tenerife's highest-rated MTB route (4.4★ AllTrails, 70 reviews). Technical trails through Anaga Rural Park's monteverde — UNESCO World Heritage. Evergreen forest, mist and deep ravines. Demanding level. Access from Cruz del Carmen via TF-12. MTB only. Helmet required.
bici-anaga-cruz-carmen.cat: MTB Anaga · Cruz del Carmen · ★ Top

bici-chinyero-ruta.desc: Unique MTB route through Chinyero Nature Reserve in the Corona Forestal. Trails through pines on grey volcanic ground — visually unique worldwide. Near Teide. Moderate-high level. Access from Santiago del Teide. Not suitable in rain. Download map before setting off.

bici-alquiler-sur.desc: Tenerife's highest concentration of bike rental shops: road, MTB and electric. Many offer guides, maps and repairs. Check Bike Experience Tenerife (bikeexperiencetenerife.com) and Cycling in Tenerife (cyclingintenerife.com). Book in advance in high season.

bici-alquiler-norte.desc: Several bike rental and service points in the north. Ideal starting point for the Teide climb (TF-21), Anaga routes and Corona Forestal. The coastal promenade is also suitable for relaxed cycling. Repair workshops available.
bici-alquiler-norte.cat: Bike Rental · Puerto de la Cruz · North

bici-agua-la-esperanza.desc: Key stop for cyclists in the north. Drinking water, picnic tables and toilets in pine forest at 1,000 m. Usual start or stop on BC-1 and the Teide climb. Free parking. Access via TF-24. Cool temperatures — bring a layer.

bici-agua-vilaflor.desc: Vilaflor (1,400 m), one of Spain's highest villages — a must-stop for cyclists on south-Teide routes. Water fountains, bars and parking. BC-5 starting point. Cool climate, clean air.

bici-ruta-medano-teide.desc: One of Tenerife's most complete road routes: from El Médano (sea level) climbing via Arafo to Teide, 4,400+ m elevation gain. Radically different landscapes: arid coast, mid-slopes, pines, volcano. For very fit cyclists only. TF-28 and TF-21. Best in winter or spring.

bici-paseo-sur.desc: The seafront promenade linking Los Cristianos to Las Américas and Costa Adeje: one of the few coastal stretches in Tenerife for relaxed cycling. Flat tarmac. Ideal for e-bikes, city or leisure bikes. ~5 km. Best early morning before pedestrian crowds. Always give way.

bici-ruta-norte-garachico.desc: 54 km circular road route from Garachico (TF-421) returning via TF-42. Rugged mountain terrain through historic villages and vineyards. For fit cyclists only. ~3 hours. Best in autumn-winter.

bici-ruta-norte-buenavista.desc: 75 km road route crossing the north of Tenerife from tip to tip: Buenavista del Norte (TF-42) to Punta del Hidalgo (TF-13). Varied terrain with few extreme ramps, and the lush green coastal landscapes of the north. Estimated time: 3h 25min. One of the most recommended routes for intermediate to advanced cyclists.

bici-circular-santa-cruz.desc: Popular 52 km circular route among cyclists from the capital. It starts at Plaza de España (TF-11), loops around the metropolitan area with coastal and mid-altitude sections, and returns to the start. Estimated time: 2h 35min. Good road surface and signposting. Ideal for local cyclists and cycling tourists based in Santa Cruz.

bici-alquiler-medano-bikepoint.desc: Top road, MTB, gravel and e-bike rental specialists in south Tenerife. Free downloadable Strava routes. Buy option: 100% rental credited toward purchase. Av. José Miguel Galván Bello 28, El Médano. Closed Sundays.

bici-alquiler-triciclos-sc.desc: High-end bike rental in north Tenerife: road, MTB, gravel and urban bikes. Santa Cruz shop. Hours: Mon–Fri, closes 13:00 reopens 16:30. Closed weekends. Weekend rentals returned Monday 10:00.

bici-alquiler-triciclos-sursula.desc: Second Triciclos Canarias location in north Tenerife, Santa Úrsula. Road, MTB, gravel and urban bikes. Mon–Fri only. Closed weekends. Great base for cyclists staying in Puerto de la Cruz or La Orotava.

bici-mtb-teno-erjos.desc: MTB route through the Teno Massif, one of the island's most spectacular. Starting in the small village of Erjos, following the twisting bends of western Teno. Dark silhouettes of the Montana Negras to the east. Dense forest, technical trails. Expert MTB riders only.

bici-mtb-arico-volcan.desc: MTB from Arico toward Charco del Pino through the ring forest near the large craters. Spectacular volcanic landscape with views to Teide's slopes. One of the island's most exciting routes to experience its wild volcanic side.

bici-puerto-bailadero.desc: One of Tenerife's most famous and beautiful mountain passes. 11 km climb from San Andrés (sea level) to 677 m via TF-12 and TF-123. 660 m elevation gain, constant 6% gradient. Hairpin bends with spectacular views over the Anaga Massif and Taganana village. Flora changes dramatically from coastal to laurel forest. Warning: no water points during the entire climb — bring enough. Summit at Mirador El Bailadero.

bici-puerto-pico-ingles.desc: Cycling ascent to Pico del Inglés (990 m), one of the highest peaks in Santa Cruz de Tenerife municipality, in the Anaga Massif. Start from San Andrés via TF-12, continuing on TF-114 to the viewpoint. Narrow winding road through thousands of trees, almost no traffic. From the summit: 360° views — Santa Cruz, Teide, Gran Canaria and La Palma on clear days. Coordinates verified by OpenStreetMap and Wikipedia.
bici-puerto-pico-ingles.cat: Mountain Pass · Anaga · 990 m altitude · TF-114

bici-evento-vuelta-teide.desc: Starting point of the Vuelta al Teide, Tenerife's most important UCI-ranked GranFondo cycling event. Held annually in spring (April-May). Three distances: GranFondo 182 km / 4,600 m elevation, MedioFondo 86 km / 1,700 m, FondoCorto 64 km / 1,300 m. Start and race pack collection at Lago Martiánez area, Puerto de la Cruz. Official website: vteide.com
bici-evento-vuelta-teide.cat: Cycling Event · GranFondo UCI · Puerto de la Cruz

ar-la-caldera.desc: One of Tenerife's most complete recreational areas, in the heights of La Orotava (1,200 m) in an ancient volcanic crater. Canarian pine and cloud forest. Free BBQ grills, tables, bar-restaurant, playground, toilets, campsite (permit required). Access: TF-21 km 16.2 or bus 345/346. Bring your own charcoal/wood. Portable BBQs banned. Fires only until 20:00 in summer.

ar-fuente-fria.desc: Cabildo recreational area in the El Sauzal highlands, within the Corona Forestal Natural Park. Barbecue pits, tables, water and toilets. A good starting point for trails. Group booking on Tenerife ON.

ar-las-lagunetas.desc: Recreational area at around 1,200 m on the Pinolere slope (Santa Úrsula), in the Las Lagunetas Protected Landscape. Fayal-brezal heath with Canary pine and views over the Orotava Valley. Barbecue pits, tables, water, toilets and a playground. Reached by a dirt track (4x4 recommended) or on foot. Group booking on Tenerife ON.

ar-ramon-caminero.desc: Recreational area above 1,500 m on the north slope, with spectacular sea-of-clouds views. Canarian pine forest. Free BBQ grills, tables, toilets and parking. Access via TF-21. Bring your own charcoal/wood.

ar-chanajiga.desc: Popular recreational area in Los Realejos, Corona Forestal Natural Park. 400 capacity. Free BBQ grills, tables, toilets, parking and playground. Trail and cycling starting point.

ar-las-raices.desc: Tenerife's largest recreational area with 56 tables, in El Rosario, Monte de La Esperanza. Famous site of the historic Pacto de Las Raíces (1936). Ancient pine forest. Free BBQ grills, toilets and parking.
ar-las-raices.cat: Free BBQ · El Rosario · 56 tables · Largest

ar-lomo-la-jara.desc: Recreational area in Tacoronte, Las Lagunetas Protected Landscape. 31 tables. Free BBQ grills, toilets and parking. Pine and cloud forest.

ar-las-calderetas.desc: Recreational area in El Sauzal, Las Lagunetas Protected Landscape. 31 tables. Free BBQ grills, toilets and parking. Pine forest with views over the island's north.

ar-la-tahona.desc: Recreational area in San Juan de la Rambla, Corona Forestal Natural Park. 38 tables. Free BBQ grills, toilets and parking.
ar-la-tahona.cat: Free BBQ · San Juan de la Rambla · 38 tables

ar-arenas-negras.desc: Spectacular recreational area in Garachico on black volcanic soil — from the last eruption of Trevejo volcano (1706). The contrast between centuries-old pines and dark volcanic terrain is unique. 400 capacity. Free BBQ grills, toilets, parking and hiking/cycling trails. Forest track access.

ar-san-jose-llanos.desc: Recreational area in El Tanque, Teno Rural Park. 38 tables. Free BBQ grills, toilets and parking. Pine forest with views over the Teno Massif. Very peaceful northwest location.
ar-san-jose-llanos.cat: Free BBQ · El Tanque · Teno Rural Park

ar-el-lagar.desc: Recreational area in Icod de los Vinos highlands, Corona Forestal. 24 tables. Free BBQ grills, toilets and parking. Pine forest near the historic vineyards of Icod.
ar-el-lagar.cat: Free BBQ · Icod de los Vinos · 24 tables

ar-las-hayas.desc: Recreational area in the highlands of Icod de los Vinos, Corona Forestal. 20 tables. Free BBQ grills. May be temporarily closed — check tenerifeon.es first.
ar-las-hayas.cat: Free BBQ · Icod de los Vinos · 20 tables

ar-chio.desc: One of Tenerife's largest with 650 capacity, in Guía de Isora under the volcanic pine forest of Chío. Free BBQ grills, tables, toilets and parking. Spectacular volcanic landscape with sea views and La Gomera.
ar-chio.cat: Free BBQ · Guía de Isora · 650 capacity

ar-los-frailes.desc: Recreational area in Arafo at 900 m, at the head of the Güímar Valley. 38 tables. Free BBQ grills, toilets and parking. Pine forest on the southeast slope. Very peaceful and well maintained.

ar-las-lajas.desc: Recreational area in Vilaflor (1,400 m), Spain's highest village, within Corona Forestal Natural Park. 42 tables. Free BBQ grills, toilets and parking. Beautiful ancient pine forest. Ideal base for Teide.

ar-los-pedregales.desc: Recreational area in Buenavista del Norte, Teno Rural Park. 20 tables. Free BBQ grills, toilets and parking. Northwest of the island with Atlantic Ocean views.
ar-los-pedregales.cat: Free BBQ · Buenavista del Norte · Teno Park

ar-llano-viejos.desc: Recreational area in La Laguna, Anaga Rural Park. 15 tables. Free BBQ grills, toilets and parking. Ancient laurel forest. Much appreciated by La Laguna residents.
ar-llano-viejos.cat: Free BBQ · La Laguna · Anaga Park

ar-la-quebrada.desc: Recreational area in Tegueste, Anaga Rural Park. 18 tables. Free BBQ grills, toilets and parking. Laurel forest and pine in the Anaga mountains. Very peaceful.

ar-hoya-abade.desc: Recreational area in La Victoria de Acentejo, Corona Forestal. 25 tables. Free BBQ grills, toilets and parking. Pine forest in the mid-altitude north.
ar-hoya-abade.cat: Free BBQ · La Victoria de Acentejo

ar-el-contador.desc: Recreational area in Arico, Corona Forestal, southeast slope. 30 tables. Free BBQ grills, toilets and parking. May be temporarily closed — check tenerifeon.es first.

ar-los-brezos.desc: Recreational area in Candelaria, Anaga Rural Park. 20 tables. Free BBQ grills, toilets and parking. Laurel forest and Canarian heather on the east slope of Anaga.

pp-taucho.desc: Tenerife's most popular paragliding take-off at 760 m in Adeje. Ideal for tandem beginners: stable trade winds, good thermals, spectacular views of Barranco del Infierno and the Costa Adeje coastline. Usual landing at Taucho-Armeñime esplanade or La Caleta beach. Best season: September to May. Certified tandem flights available year-round. Approx. price: 90–130€/person.
pp-taucho.cat: Paragliding · South Launch · 760 m · Tandem for all

pp-ifonche.desc: Take-off at 1,100 m between Adeje and Vilaflor. Higher and more technical than Taucho. Flights over the 'Dedos', Montaña El Conde and Barranco del Infierno with impressive views of the Adeje coast. Suitable for intermediate level and longer flights. Landing at Playa de la Enramada (La Caleta).

pp-izana.desc: Tenerife's most spectacular paragliding take-off: 2,200 m altitude in Teide National Park, between km 33 and 34 of TF-24. One of the highest-altitude tandem flights in Europe — landing at sea level in Puerto de la Cruz or the east coast. Views of Teide, the caldera and the Orotava and Güímar valleys. Licensed pilots or tandem with specialist schools only. Very variable conditions: always check before flying.
pp-izana.cat: Paragliding · Teide Summit · 2,200 m · Experts/Specialist Tandem Only

pp-la-corona.desc: North Tenerife paragliding take-off at 765 m in Los Realejos. Used when wind comes from North or East. Views over the Orotava Valley, Puerto de la Cruz and the north Atlantic. Landing at Finca Los Quintos or Playa del Socorro. Best season: autumn, spring and summer. Typical north trade winds. Level: beginner-intermediate in early/late hours, intermediate-advanced at midday.
pp-la-corona.cat: Paragliding · North Launch · 765 m · Los Realejos

pp-el-tanque.desc: Paragliding take-off in El Tanque (Tierra del Trigo), northwest Tenerife, around 600 m altitude. Recently renovated with improved safety features. Very popular with local pilots. Views over the Teno Massif, the Atlantic and La Palma on clear days. Typical westerly wind.
pp-el-tanque.cat: Paragliding · NW Launch · ~600 m · El Tanque

pp-guimar.desc: Paragliding flying area on Tenerife's east slope, Güímar municipality. Approx. altitude 700 m. Used when winds come from East, South or Northwest. Season: autumn to spring, and often in summer. Views over the Güímar Valley and the Atlantic. Also flown from Fasnia and Fasnia Volcano. Typical area for intermediate level pilots.

faro-teno.desc: Tenerife's most iconic lighthouse, on the far northwest tip. Built in 1897, it stands on the dramatic Teno cliffs 70 m above the sea. Access via the spectacular narrow TF-445 road (residents and public transport only) winding through mountains. From the lighthouse, epic views toward La Gomera and Los Gigantes. Protected marine ecosystem with dolphins and turtles.

faro-anaga.desc: Located at Punta de Anaga, Tenerife's northeastern tip. Built in 1863, one of the oldest lighthouses in the Canary Islands. Surrounded by ancient laurel forest and vertical cliffs of Anaga Rural Park. Access on foot only from Chamorga (about 45 min). Views over Caleta, La Rambla and Anaga's wild coast.

faro-rasca.desc: Lighthouse at the southwestern tip, within the Montaña Roja Special Nature Reserve. Built in 1972. Area of special marine interest: one of the best spots in Tenerife for whale watching (pilot whales, bottlenose dolphins). Arid, volcanic and strikingly beautiful landscape. Walk from El Médano or Playa Diego Hernández.

faro-abona.desc: The tallest lighthouse in the Canary Islands at 193 m above sea level. Built in 1895 in the southeast, in Arico municipality. White 28 m tower visible from great distances. Surrounded by black volcanic malpaís and open sea views. Scuba diving and surf area. Free access via track from TF-1.

faro-punta-hidalgo.desc: Avant-garde lighthouse at Tenerife's northeast tip, by Punta del Hidalgo (La Laguna). Built in 1992 and operational since 1994. The tallest on the island at 50 metres and one of the tallest in the Canaries. Striking angular design: irregular white columns of increasing height on a triangular base. Surrounded by greenhouses, at the end of a path. Views of Roque de Dentro, Roque de Fuera and the Anaga massif. Next to the village's natural pools.

ciudad-santa-cruz.desc: Capital of Tenerife and the province. Vibrant city with the famous Carnival (world's 2nd largest), Calatrava Auditorium, García Sanabria Park and lively Castillo Street. Busiest cruise port in the Canaries.

ciudad-laguna.desc: UNESCO World Heritage City. First planned city of the Atlantic, model for American colonial cities. University, student atmosphere, cathedral, historic streets and the best tapas on the island.

ciudad-puerto-cruz.desc: The north's premier tourist city. Manrique's Playa Jardín, Loro Parque, Lake Martiánez, colonial streets and the best cultural offer in the north. Excellent microclimate year-round.

ciudad-orotava.desc: Colonial town with the most authentic Canarian architecture. Famous for flower carpets at Corpus Christi. Casa de los Balcones, Town Hall gardens and panoramic views of the Orotava Valley with Teide in the background.

ciudad-adeje.desc: Municipality home to Costa Adeje and the tourist south. Adeje village has a charming old town with the Santa Úrsula church and Barranco del Infierno. Tenerife's most visited municipality.

ciudad-arona.desc: Municipality encompassing Los Cristianos and Las Américas. Arona village in the midlands retains its rural essence. Siam Park, Jungle Park and the south's best beaches make this the most touristic municipality.

ciudad-garachico.desc: Tenerife's most beautiful village. Former commercial capital destroyed by a volcano in 1706. El Caletón natural pools, San Miguel Castle, San Francisco Convent and Mudejar church. Unique and unrepeatable atmosphere.

ciudad-icod.desc: Famous for the Millenary Dragon Tree and red wine wineries. Well-preserved colonial architecture, Mariposas del Mundo and Cueva del Viento 5 minutes away. Tenerife's best artisanal red wine.

ciudad-candelaria.desc: Most important pilgrimage site in the Canaries. The Basilica of Our Lady of Candelaria, patron of the archipelago, receives thousands of pilgrims on 15 August. The Guanche Mencey statues on the promenade are unmissable.

ciudad-guimar.desc: Known for the Güímar Pyramids, mysterious constructions studied by Thor Heyerdahl. Fertile valley on the southeast slope of Teide. Local crafts and high-quality agricultural products.

ciudad-granadilla.desc: Southeast municipality with a very well-preserved historic centre of Granadilla Villa. El Médano and Playa La Tejita are within its boundaries. Los Abrigos port with excellent fish and seafood restaurants.

nucleo-costa-adeje.desc: Tenerife's luxury tourism zone. 5-star hotels, Playa del Duque, Playa Fañabé, spa resorts and the finest gastronomy. Siam Park is here. Quieter and more elegant than Las Américas.

nucleo-los-gigantes.desc: Village nestled beneath Spain's most impressive cliffs (up to 600 m). Marina with boat excursions to see whales and dolphins. Black sand Playa La Arena. Very calm and local atmosphere.

nucleo-puerto-santiago.desc: Quiet fishing village at the foot of Los Gigantes. Very local atmosphere, fresh fish restaurants and starting point for cliff excursions. Black sand beach with clean waters.

nucleo-callao-salvaje.desc: Quiet residential development between Adeje and Los Gigantes. Access to uncrowded beaches like Playa de la Jaquita. Quiet area with amenities for residents. Good base to explore the west coast.

nucleo-san-andres.desc: Small fishing village next to Playa Las Teresitas, Tenerife's best urban beach. Excellent fish and seafood restaurants on the promenade. 100% local atmosphere just 10 minutes from Santa Cruz.

nucleo-guia-isora.desc: Quiet municipality on the west coast, between Adeje and Los Gigantes. Alcalá and San Juan beaches with fresh fish. Abama Hotel (5-star GL). Arid and authentic landscape, no mass tourism. Starting point for the Masca trail.

nucleo-la-caleta.desc: Small fishing village in Costa Adeje famous for its fine dining restaurants. Internationally recognised chefs. Quiet and authentic beach a stone's throw from the 5-star hotel zone. The best kept secret of the south.

ciudad-tacoronte.desc: Capital of Tenerife red wine. Tacoronte-Acentejo Denomination of Origin, the Canaries' oldest. Santa Catalina Church, colonial historic centre and the island's best guachinches in its midlands.

ciudad-tegueste.desc: Rural and wine-growing municipality between La Laguna and Anaga. Preserves authentic Canarian traditions. San Marcos festivals in April with dances and traditional Mago costumes. Unique high-altitude white wines. No coast but rural charm intact. Well connected to La Laguna by bus.

ciudad-realejos.desc: Northern municipality famous for the most spectacular patron festivities in the Canaries: 3rd May fireworks. Cradle of Canarian pyrotechnics. Rambla de Castro, green landscapes and views of Teide.

ciudad-sauzal.desc: Village with one of the most beautiful viewpoints over the ocean. Casa del Vino de Canarias, museum and restaurant with the island's best wine selection. Well-kept historic centre and perfect colonial square.

ciudad-matanza.desc: Historic site where the Guanches defeated the conquistadors in 1494. Wine-growing area with traditional guachinches, wrinkly potatoes, smoked cheese and country red wine. Spectacular ocean views.

ciudad-victoria.desc: Village where the conquistadors took revenge in 1495. Today a peaceful land of vineyards, fruit trees and family guachinches. Canarian pine forest in the midlands. Stronghold of local traditions.

ciudad-santa-ursula.desc: Municipality with one of the most famous viewpoints: Humboldt Viewpoint, from where Alexander von Humboldt admired the Orotava Valley. Restaurants with spectacular views and the island's best grilled meat.

ciudad-san-juan-rambla.desc: Small coastal village in the north with colonial historic centre and natural pools. Charco de la Laja, one of Tenerife's most photographed natural pools. Bananas, wine and total tranquillity.

ciudad-guancha.desc: Rural municipality between Teide and the sea. Banana plantations on the coast, vineyards and fruit trees in the midlands, pine forests up to the national park. Stately houses, totally local atmosphere and authentic family guachinches.

ciudad-silos.desc: Green and humid village of Isla Baja. Banana plantations, laurel forest and mountain. Famous International Storytelling Festival in December. Charming colonial square, baroque church and many houses with Canarian balconies.

ciudad-buenavista.desc: Far northwestern municipality, gateway to Teno Rural Park. Designer golf course, Teno Lighthouse, Las Arenas beach and Tenerife's most virgin and green landscapes. Access to Masca from the north.

ciudad-tanque.desc: Small midland municipality between Garachico and Santiago del Teide. Pine forests, vineyards and a unique viewpoint towards the Los Gigantes cliffs and Isla Baja. Land of award-winning artisanal goat cheese.

ciudad-santiago-teide.desc: Municipality including Masca, Tamaimo, Puerto Santiago and Los Gigantes. Quiet mountain village at 925 m altitude, ideal starting point for hiking trails. Chinyero volcano, last eruption 1909. Strong rural tourism.

ciudad-vilaflor.desc: Spain's highest village at 1,400 m. Pure air, ancient pine forests and unique high-altitude wines. Southern gateway to Teide National Park. Famous for chestnuts, almond trees and the best Canarian pines.

ciudad-san-miguel.desc: Southern municipality with charming historic centre and tourist coastal area (Golf del Sur, Amarilla Golf, Costa del Silencio). Authentic mix of traditional Canarian village and tourist developments with golf courses.

ciudad-arico.desc: Southeastern municipality, Tenerife's largest. Arid landscape, volcanic malpaís and the virgin Los Abrigos beach. Punta de Abona Lighthouse, the Canaries' tallest. Sky reserve, ideal for astronomy.

ciudad-fasnia.desc: Small southeastern municipality with black volcanic landscape. Fasnia Volcano (last eruption 1705) marks the area. Rocky beaches like Los Roques and warm water year-round. Very local, no mass tourism.

ciudad-arafo.desc: Village in the Güímar Valley known as the 'Town of Music' for its century-old musical tradition. Bands, brass bands and folk groups. Almond blossoms in February, award-winning artisanal honey and midland white wine.

ciudad-rosario.desc: Midland municipality between Santa Cruz and La Laguna. La Esperanza Forest with pine and laurel forests. Las Raíces Viewpoint, where Franco prepared the 1936 uprising. Fresh air, mystical mist and trails. On the coast lies Radazul, with a marina and a beach.

nucleo-bajamar.desc: Northern coastal village famous for its huge seawater natural pools (built in the 60s). Quiet and very local atmosphere. Former summer resort for La Laguna residents. Excellent fish restaurants on the promenade.

nucleo-punta-hidalgo.desc: The last coastal village accessible by car on Anaga's north coast. Iconic lighthouse, natural pools with waves, rocks rising from the sea and the start of the Chinamada trail. Essential to discover the most authentic Anaga.

nucleo-taganana.desc: Village in Anaga's green heart, accessed via a winding road through laurel forest. Traditional houses clinging to the slope, terraced vineyards and two nearby beaches: Almáciga and Benijo. UNESCO Biosphere Heritage.

nucleo-igueste-san-andres.desc: Anaga village at the end of a deep valley, near Las Teresitas. 100% local atmosphere, time stood still, banana terraces and palm trees. Starting point for spectacular trails to hidden beaches like Antequera.

nucleo-tejina.desc: Rural agricultural village in northern La Laguna. Famous for the Tejina Hearts Festival (September, UNESCO World Heritage), spectacular folk tradition unique in the world. Green meadows and banana plantations.

nucleo-valle-guerra.desc: Rural village between Tegueste and Tacoronte. Meadows, banana plantations, vineyards and the Peasant House Museum. Totally agricultural atmosphere, no tourist presence. Exquisite local produce and Tenerife's best avocados.

nucleo-mesa-mar.desc: Small coastal area of Tacoronte with large natural pools carved into volcanic rock. Very quiet and local residential atmosphere. The pools are a refuge for La Laguna residents in summer. No tourist services.

nucleo-realejo-bajo.desc: Historic centre of Los Realejos with Tenerife's oldest church (Santiago Apóstol, 1496). Traditional Canarian atmosphere, plaza with centuries-old trees and 17th-century stately mansions. Historic-artistic heritage.

nucleo-la-ranilla.desc: Historic fishing quarter of Puerto de la Cruz. Colourful houses, traditional Canarian restaurants, alternative nightlife and the best area for fish tapas. Bohemian and artistic atmosphere, without tourist crowds.
nucleo-la-ranilla.cat: Fishing Quarter · Puerto de la Cruz

nucleo-las-galletas.desc: Southern fishing village, part of Costa del Silencio. Very popular Tuesday and Saturday market. Small marina, fresh fish restaurants at good prices. Mixed local/foreign residential atmosphere.

nucleo-costa-silencio.desc: Quiet development at the far south. No tourist crowds despite its strategic location. Residential for European retirees and locals. Easy access to airport and Los Cristianos. Popular diving spot.

nucleo-golf-del-sur.desc: Tourist development built around a 27-hole golf course. Amarilla Beach with unique volcanic tones. Apartments, hotel complexes and international restaurants. Very British in lifestyle.

nucleo-amarilla-golf.desc: Development with an 18-hole golf course designed by Donald Steel, by the sea. Sports marina with yacht club. Quiet residential and holiday resort, no nightclubs or noise. Views of La Gomera.

nucleo-playa-san-juan.desc: Authentic fishing village on the west coast. Very popular Wednesday market. Small black sand beach with calm waters. Fresh fish restaurants at local prices. 100% Canarian atmosphere without mass tourism.

nucleo-playa-paraiso.desc: Small tourist hub between Costa Adeje and Los Gigantes. Hard Rock Hotel, holiday complexes and restaurants. Natural cove sheltered by cliffs and crystal-clear waters. Access to Playa Diego Hernández by trail.

nucleo-torviscas.desc: Hub integrated into Costa Adeje. Lower Torviscas Beach with sand and complete services. Very active commercial area with shopping centres and restaurants of all nationalities. Vibrant life at any time.

faro-puerto-cruz.desc: Tenerife's most visited lighthouse, in the heart of Puerto de la Cruz, west of the fishing harbour. Built in 1995, operational since 1996. Modern square black design with an inner cylindrical tower in red and white bands. 27 metres tall, focal height 31 m above sea level, 16-nautical-mile range. Easily accessible by car with parking next to it, though the interior is closed to the public.
faro-puerto-cruz.cat: Modern Lighthouse · Puerto de la Cruz

faro-abona-viejo.desc: The original Punta de Abona lighthouse, built in 1902, which operated until replaced by the current lighthouse in 1978. The classic white Canarian-style tower remains standing as a historic element beside the modern lighthouse. One of the most solitary and beautiful spots on the south-east coast. Access via track from Abades road — high-clearance vehicle recommended.

faro-santa-cruz-puerto.desc: Lighthouse at the entrance to the Port of Santa Cruz de Tenerife, the largest port in the islands. White cylindrical tower with red band on the breakwater. Guides the large cruise ships and cargo vessels entering the port. Not normally visited but very photographed from the Maritime Park and the Auditorium.
faro-santa-cruz-puerto.cat: Port Lighthouse · Santa Cruz de Tenerife

faro-los-cristianos.desc: Small lighthouse in Los Cristianos port, from where ferries depart to La Gomera and La Palma. Compact white tower at the end of the breakwater. Photographic spot with views over Los Cristianos bay and the horizon where La Gomera is visible on clear days.

faro-garachico.desc: Small historic lighthouse in the old port of Garachico, the most beautiful village in north Tenerife. The port was partially destroyed by the 1706 volcanic eruption that buried the town with lava. The current lighthouse marks the entrance to the volcanic natural pools that have made this one of the most unique spots on the island.

camel-park.desc: First camel breeding centre in Tenerife, open since 1988. Canarian farm between Chayofa and La Camella with 20-min camel rides on volcanic trails. Farm with donkeys, goats, parrots and other rescued animals. 10 min from Los Cristianos.

mariposario-drago.desc: Spain's first centre dedicated exclusively to butterflies, opened in 1997. Tropical greenhouse where over 800 exotic butterflies from Malaysia, Costa Rica, Australia and Papua fly freely. From 2 cm species to giants of 30 cm. Visible lab with caterpillars and chrysalises. Next to the Millennial Drago Tree in Icod.
mariposario-drago.cat: Butterfly House · Icod de los Vinos

vet-medivet-sanantonio.desc: Veterinary hospital of the Medivet group, 24h care 365 days. Minimally invasive surgery, dermatology, cardiology, endoscopy, oncology. Reference centre in the Santa Cruz metropolitan area.

vet-cruz-piedra.desc: Reference veterinary hospital in La Laguna with 24h emergencies, operating theatre, permanent on-site hospitalisation, in-house lab and home service. Care for small animals and exotics.

vet-hosvetnorte.hours: 24h emergency · First veterinary hospital in Tenerife (1988)
vet-hosvetnorte.desc: Tenerife's first veterinary hospital, founded in 1988. 24h care in La Orotava, near Alcampo La Villa shopping centre. Full service, dog grooming and shop. Accessible.

vet-patas-colas.desc: 24h reference veterinary hospital in southern Tenerife. Founded in 2007 as a clinic and 24h hospital since 2014. Specialists in small animals and exotics. Cardiology, oncology, surgery and treatment financing.

vet-hospital-santa-cruz.desc: Veterinary hospital in Santa Cruz with 24-hour emergency and hospitalisation services. Operating theatre, ultrasound, ophthalmology and in-house lab. Affiliated with insurance providers.

vet-masvet-chafiras.desc: Modern veterinary hospital in Las Chafiras (south Tenerife) with 24h care, separate areas for dogs and cats, feline waiting room with pheromones. Specialty consultations, emergency and preventive care. Young, highly-rated team.

playa-cabezo.desc: Official dog beach in Güímar, the first in Tenerife. Dark volcanic sand, dog zone of around 200m with calm waters. Open 365 days a year. Parking, showers and toilets nearby.

playa-confital.desc: Dog friendly beach in Granadilla de Abona, also known as Playa del Horno. Dark volcanic sand and semi-urban natural environment. Pet access permitted all year round without time restrictions.

playa-puertito-guimar.desc: Urban beach in Puertito de Güímar with delimited dog zone. Volcanic sand, very calm waters ideal for dogs. Very accessible, even for people with reduced mobility.

playa-callao-arona.desc: Volcanic sand beach in Arona with a designated dog area. Uncrowded natural setting, ideal for pets that enjoy nature and swimming.

parque-garcia-sanabria-pet.desc: The largest urban park in Tenerife in Santa Cruz. Designated dog area, lush gardens, sculptures and fountains. Perfect for walks with pets in the city. Dogs must be on a lead in general areas.

parque-anaga-petfriendly.desc: ⚠️ Dogs are allowed only on official trails and always on a leash: protected natural area with sensitive endemic wildlife; violations are fined. Anaga Rural Park allows dogs on leads on its trails. Ancient laurisilva forest, Biosphere Reserve. Impressive ravine and cliff landscapes. A unique experience for nature lovers and their pets.

playa-las-bajas.desc: Beach with designated dog area in Arona. Dark volcanic sand and easy access. Quiet and uncrowded, ideal for dogs that enjoy swimming.

parque-la-granja-sct.desc: Dog park in the centre of Santa Cruz de Tenerife with stainless steel fenced area, separated for large and small dogs. Includes water bowls, play areas and special pet access.

parque-el-montillo.desc: Modern dog park in La Matanza, north Tenerife, opened in 2019. Canine sports circuit with agility, slalom, tunnel, ladder and ramp. One of the best equipped on the island.

parque-tabaiba-baja.desc: Dog park in Tabaiba Baja neighbourhood, Santa Cruz. Pet-friendly space with agility circuit. Ideal for pets to run and socialise in a safe fenced environment.

acc-playa-las-vistas.desc: Tenerife's most accessible beach, in Los Cristianos. Ramps, wooden walkways to the shore, adapted shade areas, amphibious chairs, transfer hoist and assisted bathing service. Adapted toilets and showers. Assisted bathing is usually available from 11:00 to 14:00 and from 15:00 to 18:00.

acc-playa-los-cristianos.desc: Urban beach with reserved parking, ramp access, walkways, adapted showers and toilets, rest area and bathing support. Los Cristianos is one of Europe's most adapted resorts.

acc-playa-troya.desc: In Las Américas. Reserved parking, ramps, walkways, amphibious chairs and crutches, adapted showers and toilets, rest area and assisted bathing.

acc-playa-torviscas.desc: Costa Adeje. Reserved parking, ramp, walkways, amphibious chairs and crutches, adapted showers and toilets, rest area and bathing support.

acc-playa-fanabe.desc: Costa Adeje. Ramp access, walkways, amphibious chairs and crutches, adapted showers and toilets, rest area and assisted bathing service.

acc-playa-duque.desc: Costa Adeje. Reserved parking, ramp, walkways, amphibious chairs and crutches, adapted showers and toilets, rest area and bathing support.

acc-playa-teresitas.desc: Santa Cruz's great golden beach has adapted access and Red Cross assisted bathing with amphibious chairs in the summer season.

acc-playa-poris.desc: In Porís de Abona (Arico). Reserved parking, ramp, walkways, amphibious chairs and crutches, adapted showers and toilets, rest area and bathing support. Quiet and uncrowded.

acc-sendero-sentidos.desc: At Cruz del Carmen (Anaga). Its first section is adapted for wheelchairs: a sensory walk through the World Heritage laurel forest. Accessible visitor centre.

acc-adissur.desc: Association supporting people with functional diversity and their families, in Tejina de Isora (Guía de Isora). Inclusive leisure and free-time activities, Saturday excursions, adapted sport, speech therapy, respite care and family support. Tel: 699 00 55 26 · trabajosocialtenerife@adissur.com

acc-loro-parque.desc: The famous Puerto de la Cruz park is fully accessible: ramps throughout, adapted toilets and trained staff. One of the island's most comfortable wheelchair visits.
acc-loro-parque.cat: Accessible Park · Puerto de la Cruz

acc-siam-park.desc: Water park with a real commitment to inclusion: Fast Pass wristbands for people with autism or Down syndrome, 50% discount with 60%+ disability, free entry with total disability. Adapted facilities.

acc-teide-portillo.desc: Teide National Park by wheelchair: El Portillo Visitor Centre is fully accessible (ramps, adapted toilets, interactive exhibits), with adapted viewpoints and short accessible paths through the volcanic landscape. The cable car base has adapted facilities; check conditions before going up.

acc-paseo-cristianos.desc: Kilometres of flat, barrier-free seafront promenade linking Los Cristianos, Las Américas and Costa Adeje. Ideal for wheelchairs: terraces, views of La Gomera and access to several adapted beaches along the way.

acc-piscina-jover.desc: Natural pool accessible for reduced mobility visitors on the coast of Tejina (La Laguna). Adapted ramp and steps to the sea, flat terrace and sunbathing area, natural freshwater shower. Quiet and family-friendly. Views of Punta del Hidalgo Lighthouse and Bajamar. Nearby public car park.

acc-paseo-garachico.desc: Accessible coastal promenade in Garachico, next to El Caletón natural pools and historic centre. Smooth paving, no steps, adapted ramps. Views of Garachico Rock. Benches every 50 m. El Caletón pools also have adapted access.

parque-cuchillitos-tristan.desc: Fenced dog area in Cuchillitos de Tristán Park, Ofra-Costa Sur district of Santa Cruz. Gravelled enclosed space where dogs can run free safely. Part of the municipality's network of 15 dog parks.

parque-don-quijote-sct.desc: Dog area in Don Quijote Park, Salud-La Salle district of Santa Cruz. Enclosed space with gravel or sand surface for pet recreation. Good location in residential area with plenty of shade.

parque-las-mantecas-laguna.desc: New dog park in Las Mantecas, La Laguna, with 900 m². Fenced with 1.5m Hercules-type fence, two access corrals, wooden benches and bins. Shaded by large ficus trees.

teide-petfriendly.desc: ⚠️ Dogs are allowed only on official trails and always on a leash: protected natural area with sensitive endemic wildlife; violations are fined. Teide National Park allows dogs on leads in free access areas and park roads. Not permitted on protected trails or inside the cable car. Essential to bring water for your pet due to altitude and heat.

parque-canino-ana-bautista.desc: Dog park in the Centro-Ifara district of Santa Cruz, next to the Ana Bautista pavilion. Fenced area for dogs to run and play. Part of Santa Cruz's network of 15 dog parks.

parque-canino-el-medano.desc: Enclosed dog area in El Médano, Granadilla. Dogs can run free. Close to pet friendly beaches La Tejita and El Confital.

parque-canino-callao-salvaje.desc: Dog area in Callao Salvaje, Adeje. Ideal for residents and tourists with pets in the southwest area.

parque-canino-playa-san-juan.desc: Dog park in Playa San Juan, Guía de Isora, near Fonsalía. Southwest Tenerife with views of the sea and La Gomera. Opened December 2018.

parque-canino-taoro.desc: Dog park next to the famous Taoro Park in Puerto de la Cruz. Green, privileged setting in northern Tenerife. Ideal for walking dogs surrounded by gardens with Atlantic views.
parque-canino-taoro.cat: Dog Park · Puerto de la Cruz

paseo-maritimo-costa-adeje.desc: Costa Adeje promenade from La Caleta to Puerto Colón allows leashed dogs. Passes La Enramada, El Duque, Fañabé and La Pinta beaches. Perfect for long walks at sunrise or sunset.

parque-canino-puntalarga.desc: Enclosed dog area in Puntalarga, Candelaria. Space for dogs to run free on the east coast of Tenerife.

parque-canino-san-benito.desc: Dog area in San Benito neighbourhood, La Laguna. Enclosed space in a historic district of this UNESCO World Heritage City.

parque-canino-laguna-via-ronda.desc: Fenced dog park on La Laguna's Vía de Ronda ring road, one of the most used in the municipality. Large space with sand and gravel, water bowls. Accessible from La Laguna centre.
parque-canino-laguna-via-ronda.cat: Dog Park · La Laguna · Vía Ronda

mir-tajao.desc: Viewpoint next to the small fishing village of Tajao overlooking the southern volcanic coast. Spectacular sunsets.

mir-guia-isora.desc: Viewpoint in the historic centre of Guía de Isora with sea panorama and views of La Gomera and La Palma on clear days.

mir-garachico.desc: Viewpoint over the historic town of Garachico, overlooking the Caletón natural pools and the ocean.

mir-baracan.desc: Viewpoint in the Teno massif overlooking Los Gigantes cliffs from above. Mountain track access.

mir-bailadero.desc: One of Anaga's most spectacular viewpoints at the massif's highest point. Views north to the Atlantic.

mir-ermita-palmar.desc: Small viewpoint next to El Palmar chapel with views over Teno agricultural valley and northwest coastal cliffs.

mir-rambla-castro.desc: Viewpoint over the northern coast between Puerto de la Cruz and Icod. Cliffs and protected area of great natural beauty.

mercadillo-tegueste.desc: Traditional Sunday market in Tegueste square. Local fruit, vegetables and crafts. Sunday mornings.

mercadillo-tacoronte.desc: Weekly market in Tacoronte, the wine zone of the north. Saturday mornings. Local wines, cheeses, fruits and Canarian crafts.

mercadillo-los-realejos.desc: Local producers market in Los Realejos. Weekends. Flowers, plants, honey, artisan cheese and organic products.

mercadillo-puerto-cruz.desc: Farmers market in Puerto de la Cruz. Tuesdays and Saturdays. Potatoes, bananas, tomatoes, honey and plants direct from the farm.

mercadillo-san-isidro.desc: Traditional market in San Isidro (Granadilla de Abona). Sunday mornings. Popular with locals from the south.

mercadillo-orotava.desc: Craft market in the historic centre of La Orotava. Wednesdays and Saturdays. Ceramics, Canarian embroidery, honey and local products.

mercadillo-los-abrigos.desc: Market next to Los Abrigos fishing port. Sundays. Local crafts, fresh fish and authentic seaside atmosphere.

mercadillo-icod.desc: Weekly market in Icod, next to the Dragon Tree. Friday mornings. Fruits, local wines and crafts from northwest Tenerife.

surf-medano.desc: Capital of windsurfing and kitesurfing in Tenerife. Constant NE trade winds. PWA World Championship venue. Ideal for all levels.

surf-playa-socorro.desc: The best longboard wave in north Tenerife. Long and consistent waves. Surf schools in season. Dark volcanic sand.

surf-benijo.desc: High level wave at Benijo beach, Anaga massif. Experienced surfers only due to currents and power. Incomparable wild landscape.

surf-playa-jardin.desc: The peak is at the end of the beach by Castillo de San Felipe: shifting A-frame peaks over volcanic sand and rock, rides of 50 to 150 m. Works best from mid to high tide. ⚠️ When the swell is big the current turns dangerous. Volcanic beach in Puerto de la Cruz designed by César Manrique. Waves for beginners and intermediate. Surf schools. Black sand.

surf-callao-salvaje.desc: Surf spot on the west coast with consistent winter waves. Intermediate-advanced level. Less crowded than the tourist south.

mir-don-martin.desc: Anaga's most famous viewpoint at 1,024 m above the Tahodio valley. 360° views over the massif and the Atlantic. Access from TF-12 road.

mir-chipeque.desc: Viewpoint on the Teide TF-21 road with spectacular views over the Orotava Valley and the Atlantic Ocean. Very photographed. Car access.

mir-la-jardina.desc: Forest viewpoint in La Esperanza, next to the road towards Las Cañadas. Panoramic views of Santa Cruz, the sea and the northeast of the island. Picnic area.

mir-pico-flores-anaga.desc: Viewpoint at the peak of the Anaga massif with simultaneous views north (open ocean) and south (Santa Cruz). Passage point between Taganana and Chamorga.

mir-cruz-hilda.desc: Viewpoint on the Santiago del Teide to Tamaimo road with direct view of Teide, the west coast and the islands. Regular stop on south circuit tours.

mir-la-corona-guimar.desc: Viewpoint over the Güímar Valley with views of the pyramids and the east coast. Access from Güímar town centre. Area of Guanche historical tradition.

mir-archipenque.desc: The most dramatic viewpoint to see Los Gigantes cliffs. On the TF-454 road above Puerto de Santiago. Direct views of the 300-800m cliffs, Punta de Teno, La Palma and La Gomera on clear days. Small café and souvenir shop. Free parking. Spectacular sunset.

mir-punta-hidalgo.desc: Coastal viewpoint at Tenerife's northernmost tip, in La Laguna municipality. Spectacular views of the uniquely designed lighthouse (1994), Roque de los Dos Hermanos and the wild Anaga coast. Ideal for Atlantic sunsets. Natural rock pools below. Accessible by car via TF-13 or bus from La Laguna.

mir-aguaide.desc: Spectacular viewpoint in Anaga Rural Park, accessible from the hamlet of Chinamada (10 min walk). Sheer drop views to the Atlantic and Punta del Hidalgo. The edge is fenced due to rock cracks that could break off — admire from the safe area. Note: experienced hikers only. Access from Punta del Hidalgo is ~5 km on foot.
mir-aguaide.cat: Viewpoint · Anaga · On foot only · Experts

mir-chivisaya.desc: Viewpoint on the slopes of Güímar overlooking the Güímar Valley, the Güímar Badlands (protected natural space of lava flows) and Tenerife's East Coast. Surrounded by heath and faya forest. Access via local road from Güímar. Quiet and little known.

mir-los-campitos.desc: Urban viewpoint in the Los Campitos neighbourhood (Santa Cruz de Tenerife) with the best views of the capital: Auditorio de Tenerife, North Docks, Torres de Santa Cruz, Palmetum and the peaks of Anaga. Ideal at sunset and at night for urban photography. Access by car or on foot through the neighbourhood.

mir-lomo-molino.desc: Panoramic viewpoint in north Tenerife with views to the Roque de Garachico (volcanic islet), Isla Baja, the Buenavista coast and the majestic Teide in the background. Surrounded by vineyards and banana plantations. One of the most photogenic viewpoints in the northwest. Access by local road.

mir-narices-teide.desc: One of the most impressive viewpoints in Teide National Park, on the TF-38 road (Los Escanillos area, Guía de Isora). Direct view of Pico Viejo (3,135m) and the 5 km² of black lava flows from the last great eruption of 1798, which formed the 'fire mouths' known as the Narices del Teide (2,661m). On clear days you can see La Gomera, La Palma and El Hierro. Free parking. Ideal for sunrise and sunset, especially in autumn and winter. 8.4 km from the Teide Cable Car.
mir-narices-teide.cat: Viewpoint · Narices del Teide · 2,661 m · TF-38

mir-cardon-guia-isora.desc: Viewpoint in Guía de Isora municipality with panoramic views of south Tenerife: the coastline between Playa San Juan and Playa de La Arena, La Gomera on the horizon and the west coast cliffs. Surrounded by cardones (Euphorbia canariensis) — the Canary Islands' most emblematic endemic cactus. Quiet and uncrowded. Access via local road from Guía de Isora.
mir-cardon-guia-isora.cat: Viewpoint · Guía de Isora · South · Cardones

mir-rambleta-teide.desc: La Rambleta is the upper station of the Teide Cable Car at 3,555 metres altitude — the highest viewpoint in Spain accessible without hiking. 360° views over the National Park: the Teide dominating above the clouds, Pico Viejo, Las Cañadas, the caldera and on clear days all seven Canary Islands simultaneously. Access by cable car (~€14 return) from the base station at 2,356m. The Telesforo Bravo Trail to the Teide summit (45 min, permit required) departs from here. Average temperature: 5-10°C in summer, below zero in winter. Always bring warm clothing. Queues in high season can be long — buy cable car tickets online.

surf-las-americas.desc: Surf school area in front of El Veril at Playa de las Américas. Beginner and intermediate level. Controlled waters, certified instructors. The most accessible option in the south.

surf-bollullo.desc: Volcanic beach with difficult access (15 min walk down) near Puerto de la Cruz. Quality waves for intermediate surf. Black sand and virgin surroundings.

surf-punta-hidalgo.desc: Northern tip of Tenerife. Powerful winter waves. Advanced surfers only due to sea force and rocky bottoms. Spectacular landscape.

surf-almaciga.desc: Almáciga beach in Anaga Rural Park is one of north Tenerife's best surf spots for intermediate-advanced level. Beach break with left and right-handers. Works all year with north and northeast swells. Best conditions: northwest swell + southerly wind. Sand and rock bottom. Uncrowded due to remote access (Anaga road). Spectacular scenery of cliffs and laurel forest.

windsurf-el-medano.desc: El Médano on Tenerife's southeast coast (Granadilla de Abona) is the world mecca for windsurfing and kitesurfing. Consistent northeast trade winds (15-30 knots, almost daily year-round) make it one of Europe's best wind beaches. El Cabezo beach is the venue for the PWA Grand Slam World Cup Tenerife — the windsurfing world championship held each summer with 160+ windsurfers from 20+ nations (Wave and Slalom X disciplines). Wind Center Playa Surf (official PWA sponsor) offers windsurf, kitesurf, wingfoil and SUP rental on the beachfront. Lessons for all levels. El Médano is also the island's kitesurfing capital, with ideal conditions at Playa La Tejita and El Cabezo. 18,000 sports tourists per year.
windsurf-el-medano.cat: Windsurf · Kitesurf · El Médano · PWA World Cup · World Mecca

windsurf-la-tejita.desc: Playa de La Tejita, south of El Médano, is the par excellence kitesurfing zone of southeast Tenerife. Dark sand beach of 1.5 km next to Montaña Roja (Special Nature Reserve). Constant trade winds and fewer obstacles than El Cabezo. Shallow water near shore — ideal for learning kitesurfing. Marked zones for swimmers and kitesurfers. Several kitesurf centres with lessons and equipment rental operate from La Tejita. Free access and free parking. Montaña Roja in the background creates a unique landscape.
windsurf-la-tejita.cat: Kitesurfing · La Tejita · El Médano · South · Learning

windsurf-el-poris.desc: El Porís de Abona on Tenerife's southeast coast (Arico municipality) is a kitesurfing spot for advanced and expert kiters. Strong, gusty NNE (north-northeast) wind — ideal for freestyle and high jumps. No permanent school infrastructure — bring your own gear and experience. Conditions are more variable and technical than El Médano. The small harbour and volcanic rock pools make it visually very attractive. 20 minutes from El Médano via TF-1.
windsurf-el-poris.cat: Kitesurfing · El Porís · Advanced · Arico · Southeast

mercadillo-santa-cruz.desc: El Rastro de Santa Cruz, the capital’s big Sunday flea market since 1979, with over 400 stalls of second-hand goods, antiques, clothing and crafts. Since March 2025 it is held on the Avenida Marítima (the car park by Avenida de la Constitución, near the Auditorium), after leaving its historic spot next to the África Market. Sunday mornings until early afternoon.

mercadillo-la-laguna.desc: Outdoor craft and local produce market next to La Laguna Municipal Market. Saturday mornings. UNESCO World Heritage City.

mercadillo-candelaria.desc: Canarian craft market in front of the Basilica of Candelaria. Weekends. Local products, textiles and Guanche crafts next to the symbol of Tenerife.

mercadillo-medano.desc: Second-hand and craft market in El Médano. Sunday mornings in the village square. Relaxed atmosphere of the surf and local community.

mercadillo-guimar.desc: Weekly market in Güímar. Thursday mornings in the main square. Local fruit and vegetables, plants, flowers and farm products from east Tenerife.

mercadillo-los-cristianos.desc: Popular market in Los Cristianos. Sunday mornings by the port. Second-hand, crafts, clothes and souvenirs. Very lively in high season.

mercadillo-las-americas.desc: Tourist market in Playa de las Américas. Wednesdays and Saturdays. Canarian crafts, jewellery, clothes and local products in the southern tourist area.

mercadillo-costa-adeje.desc: Market on the Costa Adeje promenade. Thursdays and Sundays. Crafts, aloe vera, Canarian products and jewellery. Relaxed atmosphere by the sea.

mercadillo-arona.desc: Weekly market in the village of Arona. Saturday mornings in the square. Fruit, vegetables and local produce from the municipality. Very local atmosphere, no tourists.

mercadillo-granadilla-sur.desc: Traditional market in the historic centre of Granadilla. Tuesday mornings. Southern farm products: potatoes, tomatoes, corn and local crafts.

mercadillo-buenavista.desc: Weekly market in Buenavista del Norte, municipality at the far northwest of Tenerife. Local seasonal produce: fruit, vegetables, pulses, artisan cheeses and Canarian crafts. Very local and authentic atmosphere. Ideal for discovering the most remote north of the island.

mercadillo-garachico.desc: Market in the historic municipality of Garachico, considered one of the most beautiful villages in the Canary Islands. Agricultural produce and local crafts next to the monumental zone. Garachico is known for its El Caletón natural pools, the San Francisco Convent and its cobblestone streets. The market gives one more reason to visit this charming northern village.

mercadillo-san-miguel-abona.desc: Farmer's market in San Miguel de Abona (Av. Modesto Hernández González 42). Seasonal fresh produce, cheese, honey, bread and local crafts from south Tenerife. Very local and family atmosphere. Hours: Wednesday, Saturday and Sunday 8:00-14:00.
