mercadillo-san-miguel-abona.cat: Farmer's Market · San Miguel de Abona · South

mercadillo-arico-pueblo.desc: Farmer's market in Arico, east Tenerife municipality. Local fresh produce, seasonal fruit and vegetables, artisan cheese and honey. Quiet and authentic atmosphere. Hours: Saturday 7:00-13:00. Sundays 7:00–13:00 in El Porís de Abona (Avenida Villa de Arico).

mercadillo-los-silos.desc: Farmer's market in Los Silos (Plaza Nuestra Sra. de la Luz 9), northwest Tenerife. Fresh produce, local crafts and Ycoden-Daute-Isora wines. Very local and authentic atmosphere. Hours: Sunday 8:00-14:00.

mercadillo-la-victoria.desc: Market in La Victoria de Acentejo, north Tenerife municipality in the Acentejo district. Local agricultural produce, DO Tacoronte-Acentejo wines, cheese and crafts. Quiet rural atmosphere.
mercadillo-la-victoria.cat: Market · La Victoria de Acentejo · North

guachinche-vilaflor.desc: Traditional guachinche in Vilaflor, Spain's highest village (1,400 m). Homemade food, local wine, generous portions and excellent mojos. Popular with GR-131 hikers.

rest-tipico-el-jable.desc: Simple seafood spot by the port of Las Galletas, always packed with locals. Super-fresh daily fish and shellfish: fried octopus, baby squid, sardines and wrinkled potatoes. Fair prices.

rest-tipico-mirador-abona.desc: Cosy seaside café-restaurant in Poris de Abona, beside the beach and the Punta de Abona lighthouse. Fresh tapas, fish and local produce with the best views over the bay.

guachinche-san-juan-rambla.desc: Guachinche on the outskirts of San Juan de la Rambla with sea views. North area wine, meat in sauce, wrinkled potatoes and coriander mojo. Family atmosphere.
guachinche-san-juan-rambla.cat: Guachinche · San Juan de la Rambla

guachinche-los-silos.desc: Family-run guachinche in the hills of Los Silos, in the far northwest. Carefully made homemade Canarian food: carne fiesta, escaldón, almogrote. Rated one of the island's best. Open Thursday to Sunday.

casa-del-vino-sauzal.desc: Tenerife Wine Museum in a 17th-century rural house in El Sauzal. Covers all the island's denominations of origin: Tacoronte-Acentejo, Valle de La Orotava, Ycoden-Daute-Isora, Abona and Valle de Güímar. Wine and local cheese tasting at a reduced price. Restaurant with Teide views. Classical concerts in the courtyard in summer (July–August, alternate Tuesdays 8.30pm). Adjacent Casa de la Miel. Well signposted from the El Sauzal TF-5 exit. Buses 101 and 104.
casa-del-vino-sauzal.cat: Wine Museum · El Sauzal · North · Wine Tourism

bodega-frontos-granadilla.desc: ⚠️ Winery closed to the public: the restaurant and tours have ended; the venue only hosts occasional private events. Bodega Frontos, located in Los Blanquitos (Granadilla de Abona), is more than a winery: a wine-themed park in the heart of DO Abona. Over 540,000 m² of estate at 600 m altitude in the south. Award-winning organic production. Guided cellar and vineyard tours, tastings, Canarian restaurant and Casa Tasca for events. The complex includes architecture carved into volcanic tuff. Luengo family since 1949. Advance booking required for visits.
bodega-frontos-granadilla.cat: Winery · DO Abona · Granadilla · Wine Tourism

bodega-cueva-rey-icod.desc: One of the most emblematic wineries of DO Ycoden-Daute-Isora, in Icod de los Vinos (Camino Cueva del Rey 1). Bodegas Insulares Tenerife is the largest cooperative on the island, with over 1,000 associated growers. Guided tours of the traditional (partly underground) winery, tasting of Listán Blanco, Listán Negro and recovered local varieties, paired with Canarian cheese and charcuterie. Wine and local products shop. Advance booking for groups.
bodega-cueva-rey-icod.cat: Winery · DO Ycoden · Icod de los Vinos · Wine Tourism

zona-mariscos-los-abrigos.desc: Los Abrigos, a small fishing village in south Tenerife (Granadilla de Abona), is the island's most renowned fresh fish and seafood restaurant zone. A row of specialist restaurants facing the harbour: lobster, burgado (sea snail), limpets, sancocho canario, salted vieja (parrotfish), octopus, squid and cherne. Some have been here over 40 years. Local favourites: El Jablito, El Roque. More affordable than tourist areas. A 100% local atmosphere. Book at weekends.

super-mercadona-sct.desc: Mercadona in Santa Cruz de Tenerife. One of the cheapest supermarkets on the island. Wide selection of Canarian products. Parking available.

super-hiperdino-sct.desc: HiperDino in Santa Cruz. Reference Canarian chain, competitive prices and great variety of local island products. Fresh Canarian fruit and vegetables.

super-mercadona-laguna.desc: Mercadona in La Laguna, UNESCO Heritage city. Good prices, wide selection. Ideal for residents and tourists staying in the north.

super-hiperdino-laguna.desc: HiperDino in La Laguna. Top Canarian products, local butcher, fruiterer with island produce. Very popular with northern residents.

super-mercadona-pcruz.desc: Mercadona in Puerto de la Cruz. Affordable prices for tourists and northern residents. Close to the hotel zone. Parking.

super-hiperdino-pcruz.desc: HiperDino in Puerto de la Cruz. Reference supermarket for northern residents. Seasonal local products and fresh Canarian produce.

super-mercadona-adeje.desc: Mercadona in Adeje, one of the most visited supermarkets in the south for its price and size. Very well stocked for long-stay tourists.

super-hiperdino-adeje.desc: HiperDino in Costa Adeje. Fresh Canarian products, butcher, deli and artisan bakery. Ideal for tourists in Adeje and Fañabé.

super-mercadona-arona.desc: Mercadona in Los Cristianos. One of the busiest supermarkets in the tourist south. Reference prices. Parking.

super-hiperdino-arona.desc: HiperDino in Los Cristianos. Seasonal Canarian products, local cheeses, island wines and fresh fruit. Very competitive prices.

super-mercadona-orotava.desc: Mercadona in La Orotava. Well located for the Orotava Valley. Affordable prices for residents and tourists in north Tenerife.

super-hiperdino-icod.desc: HiperDino in Icod de los Vinos. Reference for north-west municipalities. Local products from the Ycoden-Daute-Isora wine zone.

super-hiperdino-guimar.desc: HiperDino in Güímar. Reference supermarket for the eastern area. Local fresh produce and seasonal products from the Güímar valley.

super-hiperdino-granadilla.desc: HiperDino in Granadilla de Abona. Reference for the inner south. Transit area between the tourist south and Tenerife South airport.

minimarket-24h-sct.desc: Minimarket open 24 hours in the centre of Santa Cruz. Basic products, drinks, snacks and essential items. Ideal for night emergencies.

minimarket-24h-laguna.desc: 24-hour minimarket in La Laguna, near the university area. Drinks, snacks, basic food and hygiene products. Very popular with students.

minimarket-24h-pcruz.desc: Minimarket open 24 hours in the heart of Puerto de la Cruz. Drinks, snacks and basics. Essential for tourists in the northern area.

minimarket-24h-las-americas.desc: 24-hour minimarket in Playa de las Américas. Drinks, snacks, sunscreen and beach items. Very busy in summer and at weekends.

minimarket-24h-adeje.desc: 24-hour minimarket in Costa Adeje. Cold drinks, snacks and convenience items for tourists in the premium southern zone.

turismo-sct.desc: Official tourism office of Santa Cruz de Tenerife. Maps, brochures, event information. Staff in Spanish and English. Next to Plaza de España.

turismo-cv-portillo.desc: Main visitor center of Teide National Park, at the El Portillo crossroads (~2,000 m). Exhibits on the volcano, geology and flora, a botanical garden and a starting point for trails. Free entry.

turismo-cv-telesforo.desc: Teide National Park visitor center in the town of La Orotava. A three-floor multimedia museum about Teide, volcanoes and the island's history. Free entry.
turismo-cv-telesforo.cat: Visitor Center · P.N. del Teide · La Orotava

turismo-cv-canada-blanca.desc: Teide National Park visitor center, next to the Parador (~2,100 m). Exhibition on the volcano and the park, a cinema room, a shop and a café with a terrace facing Teide. Free entry.

turismo-cv-pedregales.desc: Teno Rural Park visitor center, at Los Pedregales (Buenavista del Norte). Information and maps of the park’s trail network, with personal assistance.
turismo-cv-pedregales.cat: Visitor Center · P. Rural de Teno

turismo-cv-cruz-carmen.desc: Anaga Rural Park visitor center, at Cruz del Carmen (Las Mercedes). Exhibition on the laurel forest and Anaga's culture, trail information and maps. Next to the viewpoint and the start of several routes.
turismo-cv-cruz-carmen.cat: Visitor Center · P. Rural de Anaga

turismo-cv-masca.desc: Visitor center for the Masca Gorge trail (Santiago del Teide). It manages access and permits for the gorge trail, with information and a terrace with views. Booking is required to walk down the gorge.

turismo-laguna.desc: La Laguna UNESCO tourism office. Historic centre routes, cultural information. Multilingual staff.

turismo-pcruz.desc: Puerto de la Cruz tourism office. Information on beaches, Teide excursions and northern activities. Staff in several languages.

turismo-adeje.desc: Adeje tourism office. Information for southern tourists: Costa Adeje, Playa del Duque. Excursions, transport and activities.

turismo-los-cristianos.desc: Los Cristianos tourism office, next to the ferry port. Information on island ferries, boat excursions and southern tourist activities.

turismo-candelaria.desc: Tourism office next to the Candelaria Basilica. Information on the patron saint of the Canary Islands, the Güímar Pyramids and east Tenerife.

turismo-icod.desc: Icod tourism office next to the Dragon Tree. Information on the oldest tree in Tenerife, the Cave of the Wind and the northwest.

turismo-garachico.desc: Garachico tourism office. Information on the Caletón pools, the convent and the history of the most beautiful northern town.

camping-nauta.desc: The only private campsite open all year in Tenerife. Next to San Marcos beach in Icod. Pitches for tents, bungalows and motorhomes. Pool and restaurant.

camping-madre-agua.desc: Official Cabildo de Tenerife camp in Granadilla de Abona, in the Corona Forestal Natural Park. A remote, peaceful spot in the southern pine forest. For organised group camps (schools, associations) with prior authorisation (requested on Tenerife ON).
camping-madre-agua.cat: Group Camp · Granadilla de Abona · Cabildo

camping-barranco-arena.desc: Official Cabildo de Tenerife camp in La Guancha, in the Corona Forestal Natural Park. Shares facilities with the Nature Classroom, near El Lagar. For organised group camps (schools, associations) with prior authorisation (requested on Tenerife ON).

camping-la-caldera.desc: Official Cabildo de Tenerife camping zone in La Orotava. It lies in the Corona Forestal Natural Park. A starting point for several forest trails. Beside a recreational area with toilets, barbecue pits and water. Free camping with a prior permit (booked on Tenerife ON).
camping-la-caldera.hours: Prior permit required · book on Tenerife ON

camping-ramon-caminero.desc: Official Cabildo de Tenerife camping zone in La Orotava. It lies in the Corona Forestal Natural Park. With views over the sea of clouds. Beside a recreational area with toilets, barbecue pits and water. Free camping with a prior permit (booked on Tenerife ON).
camping-ramon-caminero.hours: Prior permit required · book on Tenerife ON

camping-las-lajas.desc: Official Cabildo de Tenerife camping zone in Vilaflor. It lies in the Corona Forestal Natural Park. High in the mountains, next to Teide National Park; habitat of the blue chaffinch. Beside a recreational area with toilets, barbecue pits and water. Free camping with a prior permit (booked on Tenerife ON).
camping-las-lajas.hours: Prior permit required · book on Tenerife ON

camping-arenas-negras.desc: Official Cabildo de Tenerife camping zone in Garachico. It lies in the Corona Forestal Natural Park. A contrast of black volcanic sand, pines and sea in the distance. Beside a recreational area with toilets, barbecue pits and water. Free camping with a prior permit (booked on Tenerife ON).
camping-arenas-negras.hours: Prior permit required · book on Tenerife ON

camping-san-jose-llanos.desc: Official Cabildo de Tenerife camping zone in El Tanque. It lies in the Corona Forestal Natural Park. With a playground and a nearby restaurant. Beside a recreational area with toilets, barbecue pits and water. Free camping with a prior permit (booked on Tenerife ON).
camping-san-jose-llanos.hours: Prior permit required · book on Tenerife ON

camping-las-hayas.desc: Official Cabildo de Tenerife camping zone in Icod de los Vinos. It lies in the Corona Forestal Natural Park. Reached by a dirt track: 4x4 recommended. Beside a recreational area with toilets, barbecue pits and water. Free camping with a prior permit (booked on Tenerife ON).

camping-la-tahona.desc: Official Cabildo de Tenerife camping zone in San Juan de la Rambla. It lies in the Corona Forestal Natural Park. Reached by a narrow, steep road. Beside a recreational area with toilets, barbecue pits and water. Free camping with a prior permit (booked on Tenerife ON).

camping-los-pedregales.desc: Official Cabildo de Tenerife camping zone in Buenavista del Norte. It lies in the Teno Rural Park. Among the palms of the Teno massif; tents only, no campervans. Beside a recreational area with toilets, barbecue pits and water. Free camping with a prior permit (booked on Tenerife ON).

camping-los-pedregales.hours: Prior permit required · book on Tenerife ON

Beside a recreational area with toilets, barbecue pits and water. Free camping with a prior permit (booked on Tenerife ON).

camping-fuente-pedro.hours: Prior permit required · book on Tenerife ON

camping-fuente-llano.hours: Prior permit required · book on Tenerife ON

camping-chio.desc: Official Cabildo de Tenerife camping zone in Guía de Isora. It lies in the Corona Forestal Natural Park. In the Chío pine forest, near the Teide access road and with a playground. Beside a recreational area with toilets, barbecue pits and water. Free camping with a prior permit (booked on Tenerife ON).

camping-chio.hours: Prior permit required · book on Tenerife ON

camping-el-lagar.desc: Official Cabildo de Tenerife camping zone in Icod de los Vinos. It lies in the Corona Forestal Natural Park. With views of Teide and forest trails. Beside a recreational area with toilets, barbecue pits and water. Free camping with a prior permit (booked on Tenerife ON).
camping-el-lagar.cat: Camping Area · Icod de los Vinos · Cabildo
camping-el-lagar.hours: Prior permit required · book on Tenerife ON

camping-las-raices.desc: Official Cabildo de Tenerife camping zone in La Esperanza. It lies in the Corona Forestal Natural Park. A starting point for several forest trails. Beside a recreational area with toilets, barbecue pits and water. Free camping with a prior permit (booked on Tenerife ON).
camping-las-raices.hours: Prior permit required · book on Tenerife ON

museo-carnaval-sct.desc: Museum dedicated to the Santa Cruz Carnival, declared of International Tourist Interest. History, costumes and photographs of the world's second most famous carnival after Rio.

casa-carta-valle-guerra.desc: 17th century manor house converted into Tenerife's Museum of Ethnography and Anthropology. Unique Canarian colonial architecture. Rural life, traditional costumes and historic utensil collections.

iglesia-concepcion-laguna.desc: The oldest church in the Canary Islands (1511). Five-storey Mudejar tower, symbol of La Laguna. Houses the Cross of the Conquest brought by Alonso Fernández de Lugo. UNESCO World Heritage alongside the city.

palacio-nava-laguna.desc: 18th-century Baroque palace, one of the most representative of Canarian civil architecture. Home to various cultural institutions. Façade with typical Canarian continuous wooden balcony. Located in La Laguna's UNESCO historic centre.

iglesia-san-agustin-laguna.desc: 16th-century Augustinian convent and church. Now home to the Higher Conservatory of Music of the Canary Islands. The nave features a beautiful Mudejar ceiling. Part of La Laguna's UNESCO World Heritage historic ensemble.

iglesia-san-marcos-icod.desc: 16th-century parish church next to the famous Millenary Dragon Tree. Notable for its Baroque altarpieces and a volcanic stone baptismal font. The tower is a landmark of the municipality. Very photogenic with the Dragon Tree in the background.

iglesia-san-juan-orotava.desc: 18th-century Baroque church in the historic heart of La Orotava. One of the most beautiful in the Canary Islands with its neoclassical volcanic stone facade. Interior with gilded altarpieces and a highly venerated Virgin of the Conception. La Orotava is one of Tenerife's most beautiful historic cities.

palacio-episcopal-laguna.desc: Headquarters of the Diocese of Tenerife in La Laguna's UNESCO historic centre. 18th-century building with a beautiful Baroque stone portal and typical Canarian wooden balconies. Facing the Cathedral, it forms part of the most important monumental ensemble in the Islands.

teatro-guimera.desc: The oldest and most important theatre in the Canary Islands, inaugurated in 1851. Neoclassical architecture with capacity for 900 people. Home to the Tenerife Symphony Orchestra and Ballet Víctor Ullate. Declared an Asset of Cultural Interest. Free entry to visit the foyer.

teatro-leal-laguna.desc: Historic modernist theatre from 1915 in La Laguna's old town. Unique modernist façade in the Canary Islands, with decorative reliefs and original lettering. Restored and active. Varied programme of theatre, dance and music throughout the year.

parroquia-san-pedro-daute.desc: 16th-century parish church in Garachico, one of the oldest in the north. Survived the 1706 volcanic eruption that buried the city. Interior with Baroque altarpieces. Next to the most spectacular volcanic coastline in the north.

super-mercadona-tacoronte.desc: Mercadona in Tacoronte, wine area. Reference prices for Tacoronte, El Sauzal and La Matanza residents. Well stocked.

super-hiperdino-tacoronte.desc: HiperDino in Tacoronte. Canarian products from the wine area. Reference for El Sauzal, La Matanza and La Victoria de Acentejo.

super-hiperdino-candelaria.desc: HiperDino in Candelaria. Reference for central-east Tenerife. Next to the Candelaria commercial area.

super-hiperdino-sauzal.desc: HiperDino in El Sauzal. Also serves La Matanza and La Victoria de Acentejo. DO Tacoronte-Acentejo products.

super-hiperdino-san-juan-rambla.desc: HiperDino in San Juan de la Rambla. Reference for the northwest coastal corridor: La Guancha and surroundings.

super-hiperdino-santiago-teide.desc: HiperDino in Santiago del Teide. The only large supermarket in the municipality. Also serves El Tanque, Los Silos and Buenavista del Norte.

super-hiperdino-arona-pueblo.desc: HiperDino in Arona village. Reference for residents of the interior of the municipality, away from the tourist coast.

super-hiperdino-san-miguel.desc: HiperDino in San Miguel de Abona. Reference for the inner south between Arona and Granadilla. Arico and Fasnia also use it.

super-hiperdino-buenavista.desc: HiperDino in Buenavista del Norte, the northwesternmost municipality. Also serves Los Silos. The northernmost supermarket on the island.

minimarket-24h-arona.desc: 24-hour minimarket in the Arona village area. Basic products, drinks and snacks for residents of the municipality interior.

mercadona-el-medano.desc: Mercadona supermarket in El Médano (Av. José Miguel Galván Bello), south Tenerife. Main reference for residents and tourists of El Médano, La Tejita, Los Abrigos and Golf del Sur. Large free car park. Fresh produce, bakery, fishmonger. Usual hours: Monday to Saturday 09:00-21:30.

hiperdino-los-realejos.desc: HiperDino supermarket in Los Realejos, in north Tenerife between Puerto de la Cruz and Icod de los Vinos. Main shopping reference for municipality residents and visitors to the north coast area.

lidl-santa-cruz.desc: Lidl supermarket in Santa Cruz de Tenerife. German discount chain with wide range, own brands and competitive prices. Bakery, fruit and veg, weekly bazaar. Free parking.

mercadona-candelaria.desc: Mercadona in Candelaria, east Tenerife. Main reference for Candelaria and Igueste residents. Large car park, fresh produce, fishmonger and bakery.

lidl-la-laguna.desc: Lidl supermarket in La Cuesta-Taco (La Laguna). Ctra. General La Cuesta-Taco km 1.1. Bakery, fruit and veg, weekly bazaar. Free parking. Mon-Sat 9:00-21:30.

lidl-puerto-cruz.desc: Lidl supermarket in Puerto de la Cruz, on the Carretera General Icod-Santa Cruz. Bakery, fresh produce, weekly bazaar, own-brand products at competitive prices. Free parking. Mon-Sat 9:00-21:30.
lidl-puerto-cruz.cat: Supermarket · Lidl · Puerto de la Cruz · North

lidl-granadilla.desc: Lidl supermarket in Granadilla de Abona, Avenida de la Democracia. Near Tenerife South Airport and El Médano. Bakery, fresh produce, weekly bazaar. Free parking. Mon-Sat 9:00-21:30.

mercadona-granadilla.desc: Mercadona in Granadilla de Abona town, south Tenerife. Reference for municipality residents. Large car park, fresh produce, fishmonger and bakery. Usual hours: Mon-Sat 9:00-21:30.

hiperdino-arona-montaneta.desc: HiperDino in La Montañeta, Arona. Shopping reference for Arona municipality residents outside tourist areas. Wide selection of Canarian products.

turismo-guimar.desc: Güímar tourism office. Information on the Güímar Pyramids, the ravine and eastern hiking routes.

turismo-orotava.desc: Tourism office in La Orotava historic centre. Information on colonial houses, gardens and the Corpus Christi flower carpets.

turismo-arona.desc: Arona municipality tourism office in Las Galletas. Information on La Tejita, Montaña Roja, Los Abrigos and southern beaches.

turismo-santiago-teide.desc: Santiago del Teide tourism office. Information on Los Gigantes, Masca and Punta de Teno. Starting point for spectacular routes.

turismo-buenavista.desc: Tourist information office for Buenavista del Norte. Information on the Teno Massif, Punta de Teno, northwest hiking routes, El Palmar and the area's viewpoints.

turismo-medano.desc: Tourist information office in El Médano (Granadilla de Abona). Area known for elite windsurfing and kitesurfing, Playa La Tejita, Montaña Roja and the volcanic south coast.

turismo-tacoronte.desc: Tourist information office for Tacoronte. Home to the oldest wine denomination of origin in the Canary Islands — Tacoronte-Acentejo. Information on wineries, guachinches, municipal festivals (San Marcos), ermitas and northern Tenerife routes.

castillo-paso-alto.desc: 17th-century fortress on Santa Cruz seafront, built to defend the city from pirate and naval attacks. One of the defence points during Admiral Nelson's famous attack in 1797. Today houses the Military History Museum of the Canary Islands. Views over the port and bay.
castillo-paso-alto.cat: Castle · Santa Cruz · Military Museum · Historic

ermita-san-telmo.desc: Small 18th-century chapel in Puerto de la Cruz, patron saint of sailors. Located next to the sea in the La Ranilla neighbourhood, it is one of the city's oldest and most picturesque chapels. The square in front has direct views of the Atlantic and volcanic rocks — one of the most photogenic spots in the north.
ermita-san-telmo.cat: Chapel · Puerto de la Cruz · Sailors · Photogenic

plaza-adelantado-laguna.desc: The historic heart of San Cristóbal de La Laguna (UNESCO World Heritage City). Square surrounded by the most emblematic buildings of the historic centre: the Town Hall, Santa Catalina Convent, Concepción Church and Casa del Corregidor. French marble fountain (1870) at the centre. First paved in 1798, landscaped since 1843. Venue for the city's main cultural events. Very local and lively atmosphere.
plaza-adelantado-laguna.cat: Historic Square · La Laguna · UNESCO Heritage

casa-salazar-laguna.desc: 17th-century Baroque palace at Calle San Agustín 28, La Laguna. Built in 1664 by the Count of Salazar. Outstanding example of Canarian Baroque with Mannerist and Neoclassical elements. Facade considered the best preserved in the Canary Islands, with two Salazar family coats of arms and zoomorphic gargoyles. Cultural Heritage Site since 1983. After a fire in 2006 only the facade remained, subsequently restored. Current seat of the Diocese of Tenerife.
casa-salazar-laguna.cat: Baroque Palace · La Laguna · BIC · Bishopric

casa-capitanes-generales.desc: Emblematic 18th-century building on Plaza de la Candelaria in Santa Cruz, built between 1741 and 1750. Served as headquarters of the Captains General of the Canary Archipelago for over a century. Baroque facade with street-level arcades. Cultural Heritage Site. Currently Santa Cruz de Tenerife City Hall. One of the finest examples of 18th-century Canarian civil architecture.
casa-capitanes-generales.cat: Captains' House · Santa Cruz · Baroque · BIC · City Hall

casa-anchieta-laguna.desc: Birthplace of Blessed José de Anchieta (1534–1597), one of the most important missionaries in the history of Brazil and South America, known as the 'Apostle of Brazil'. 16th–17th century building in La Laguna's historic centre (UNESCO). Cultural Heritage Site since 1986. In 2020 restoration began to convert it into a museum dedicated to Anchieta's life and work, with opening expected soon.

sala-westerdahl.desc: The Eduardo Westerdahl Room is the most important contemporary art space in north Tenerife, in Puerto de la Cruz. It honours Eduardo Westerdahl (1902-1983), art critic who championed Surrealism in the Canaries and corresponded with Dalí, Braque and Miró. Hosts permanent collections and temporary exhibitions.
sala-westerdahl.cat: Contemporary Art · Westerdahl · Puerto de la Cruz

museo-etnografico-granadilla.desc: Granadilla de Abona Ethnographic Museum in the historic Casa de la Aduana in the town centre. Documents local history and traditions: farming tools, domestic utensils, regional costumes, local crafts and traditional agricultural activities. Shows daily life in the south before tourism. Free or low-cost entry.
museo-etnografico-granadilla.cat: Ethnographic Museum · Granadilla de Abona · South · Free

playa-guios.desc: Black sand and volcanic pebble beach beneath the dramatic Los Gigantes cliffs. One of Tenerife's most dramatic and photogenic beaches. Crystal waters for snorkelling. No lifeguard. Access from Los Gigantes harbour (5 min walk) or by kayak.

playa-antequera.desc: One of Tenerife's most isolated and pristine beaches. Only accessible on foot via Antequera ravine (~2h from Taganana) or by boat from San Andrés. Black volcanic sand between green Anaga cliffs. No services. Crystal clear water. Bring water, food and hiking footwear.
playa-antequera.cat: Wild Beach · Anaga · On foot or boat only

playa-barqueros-buenavista.desc: Black volcanic sand beach in Buenavista del Norte, 16 minutes' walk from the village centre. Small and sheltered, with an entirely local atmosphere and few crowds. Surrounded by cliffs and palms. No services. Water sometimes rough — swim with caution. An authentic corner of northwest Tenerife.
playa-barqueros-buenavista.cat: Beach · Buenavista del Norte · Black Sand · Local

playa-la-caleta-adeje.desc: Small dark sand beach in La Caleta, Adeje. Authentic fishing village in the middle of the southern tourist area. 100% local atmosphere: fishermen's terraces, boats in the harbour, fresh seafood restaurants. 10 min drive from Costa Adeje. Much more authentic than the neighbouring tourist beaches. Lifeguarded in high season.

playa-igueste-san-andres.desc: Small pebble and black sand beach in the village of Igueste de San Andrés, in Anaga Rural Park. A quiet and very local spot, far from mass tourism. Access via TF-127 from San Andrés. Clean water but with currents — swim carefully. Good starting point for Anaga routes.
playa-igueste-san-andres.cat: Beach · Igueste de San Andrés · Anaga

wc-teide-parque.desc: Official National Park live cameras with views from the cable car stations.

wc-teide-hoy.desc: Live webcams and real-time cable car status: weather, trails and road access to Teide today.

wc-los-cristianos.desc: Los Cristianos beach and bay live.

wc-las-vistas.desc: The golden sands of Las Vistas beach live.

wc-troya.desc: Playa de Troya and the Las Américas vibe live.

wc-duque.desc: The elegant Playa del Duque in Costa Adeje live.

wc-medano.desc: Wind, waves and kites: El Médano live, a windsurfing mecca.

wc-gigantes.desc: Los Gigantes harbour and cliffs live.

wc-san-juan.desc: Playa San Juan in Guía de Isora live.

wc-martianez.desc: Lago Martiánez and the Puerto de la Cruz seafront live.

wc-garachico.desc: The El Caletón natural pools in Garachico live.

wc-punta-hidalgo.desc: Punta del Hidalgo natural pool with Bajamar and Teide in the background.

wc-teresitas.desc: The golden Las Teresitas beach and San Andrés live.

wc-benijo.desc: The roques and wild sea of Benijo, in Anaga, live.

wc-orotava.desc: La Orotava’s Town Hall square live.

wc-plaza-espana.desc: Santa Cruz’s Plaza de España live.

pk-plaza-espana.desc: Guarded multi-storey underground car park in the city centre, next to Plaza de España and the Cabildo. Direct access from the Avenida Marítima tunnel.

pk-ramon-cajal.desc: Automated four-level covered car park next to Plaza de la Concordia. Screens at the entrance show free spaces.

pk-intercambiador-sc.aviso: Free for up to 4 h if you validate a return bus or tram trip with the ten+ card.
pk-intercambiador-sc.desc: Underground car park at the central bus and tram station, run by TITSA. Access from the TF-1 motorway and Avenida Tres de Mayo.

pk-palmetum.aviso: Unofficial attendants often ask for a tip: this is not an official service and you are not obliged to pay.
pk-palmetum.desc: Large free open-air car park by the sea, shared by Parque Marítimo César Manrique and the Palmetum. Entrance from the Avenida de la Constitución roundabout.

pk-quinteras-laguna.desc: Fenced municipal surface car park, a short walk from La Laguna's historic centre. Run by the municipal company MUVISA.

pk-clubo-la-pinta.aviso: Booking ahead gets you a full-day pass for around €15.
pk-clubo-la-pinta.desc: Private underground short-stay car park next to La Pinta beach and the main entrance to Puerto Colón.

pk-oasis-americas.desc: Underground car park of the Oasis shopping centre, beneath the Avenida de las Américas shopping strip.

pk-puerto-cristianos.aviso: Mainly intended for people taking the ferry to another island and leaving the car here.
pk-puerto-cristianos.desc: Fenced, automated surface car park run by the Port Authority, right opposite the ferry terminal.

pk-tfn-p1.aviso: Booking in advance on the AENA website is considerably cheaper than paying at the barrier.
pk-tfn-p1.desc: AENA's P1 public car park, a covered multi-storey building right opposite the Tenerife North Airport terminal.

pk-muelle-puerto-cruz.aviso: Unofficial attendants often ask for a tip: this is not an official service and you are not obliged to pay.
pk-muelle-puerto-cruz.desc: Huge paved public open-air car park right on the seafront. Access from Avenida Blas Pérez González or Calle Mequinez.

pk-plaza-europa-pc.desc: Underground car park in the heart of the old town, next to the town hall and Plaza del Charco. Entrance on Calle Santo Domingo.

pk-martianez-pc.aviso: Validating a purchase at the Mercadona inside gets you discounts and free periods. Best covered option when the seafront is full.
pk-martianez-pc.desc: Spacious, well-lit underground car park beneath the Martiánez shopping centre. Entrance on Avenida Aguilar y Quesada.

pk-casco-botanico-pc.desc: Public surface car park with wide bays, in the upper part of town next to the Botanical Garden (Carretera de las Dehesas).

pk-parque-taoro-pc.desc: Public surface parking in landscaped grounds, next to the historic Parque Taoro. Entrance on Camino de la Sortija.

pk-san-agustin-orotava.aviso: The entrance on Calle Cantos Canarios is narrow.
pk-san-agustin-orotava.desc: Small private underground car park with 137 spaces in the town centre, steps from Plaza del Quinto Centenario and Casa de los Balcones.

pk-la-torrita-orotava.aviso: It sits uphill: a few minutes' walk down to the old town, and back up on the way out.
pk-la-torrita-orotava.desc: Large council-run public surface car park, open 24 hours. Access from Avenida la Torrita.

pk-orotava-centro.aviso: The internal ramps and bays are narrow.
pk-orotava-centro.desc: Private covered car park in La Orotava's old town. Direct entrance on Calle Inocencio García.

pk-los-realejos.aviso: Saves circling for a space around the open-air shopping area.
pk-los-realejos.desc: Large municipal surface car park: paved, flat and signposted. Access from Calle San Agustín.

pk-tacoronte-estacion.desc: Public open-air short-stay car park next to the main square, the starting point for the old town and the Farmers' Market. Entrance on Calle Sebastián Machado.

pk-drago-icod.desc: Six-storey covered car park with a pedestrian exit right by the Drago Milenario ticket office. Access from Avenida de Canarias.

pk-alvarez-icod.desc: Private underground garage in the town centre, next to the town hall offices. Entrance on Calle Emeterio Gutiérrez Albelo.

pk-magalona-icod.aviso: Free for customers who spend at the shopping centre's businesses.
pk-magalona-icod.desc: Spacious underground car park with a direct lift, beneath the La Magalona shopping centre. Entrance from the motorway link.

pk-campo-futbol-garachico.desc: Huge public open-air car park running along the sea, next to the football ground. Five minutes' walk from the old town. Entrance on Avenida Adolfo Suárez.

pk-garachico-casco.desc: Small public open-air car park next to the town hall, on Calle Esteban de Ponte.

pk-los-silos.desc: Public surface parking marked out with white lines, a few metres from the church square. Entrance on Calle de la Estrella.

pk-buenavista-casco.aviso: Used as the stop-off point before taking the bus up to Punta de Teno.
pk-buenavista-casco.desc: Public surface car park set up to keep cars out of the protected old town. Entrance on Calle Los Claveles.

pk-cruz-carmen-anaga.aviso: It fills up before 10:00. Arrive later and expect to circle or park far away.
pk-cruz-carmen-anaga.desc: Official open-air car park deep in the laurel forest, next to the visitor centre. Access from the Anaga ridge road (TF-12).

pk-tegueste.desc: Council-run urban surface car park serving the farmers' market and the old town. Entrance on Calle Preste Juan, next to Plaza de San Marcos.

pk-bajamar-piscinas.aviso: Very crowded in summer: by midday it is hard to find a space near the pools.
pk-bajamar-piscinas.desc: Bays and roadside spaces spread along the seafront streets, heading down Avenida Gran Poder to the promenade.

pk-juan-carlos-cristianos.desc: Large public open-air car park next to the bus interchange, the main free option so you don't drive into the pedestrian centre. Entrance on Avenida Juan Carlos I.

pk-medano-publico.aviso: Fills up fast in the morning: surfers and swimmers get there early.
pk-medano-publico.desc: Large municipal surface car park on prepared ground, at the main entrance to the village on Avenida José Miguel Galván Bello.

pk-san-miguel-golf.desc: Paved open-air car park with marked bays, for access to the coastal resorts and golf courses. Entrance on Paseo J. M. Galván Bello.

pk-plaza-duque-adeje.aviso: Usually gives the first hour free if you shop at the supermarket or the shops inside.
pk-plaza-duque-adeje.desc: Private underground car park with wide bays beneath the Plaza del Duque shopping centre. Access via the ramp on Calle Londres.

pk-los-gigantes.aviso: There is almost no space on the steep cliff streets: counting on this car park saves a lot of time.
pk-los-gigantes.desc: Private underground short-stay car park close to the marina. Access down Calle Flor de Pascua.

pk-playa-arena-santiago.aviso: White lines mean free. Avenida Marítima, Calle Ana María and Calle El Lajial. In summer and at weekends it fills up: better before 10:00. If there is no space, paid car parks at Balcón de Los Gigantes or El Mirador, 1.50-2.50 €/h.
pk-playa-arena-santiago.desc: Public marked surface car park running along the Avenida Marítima, metres from the black-sand beach access.

pk-guia-isora.desc: Open municipal car park behind the main church, a good base before walking the old town or heading out on the trails. Entrance on Calle de San Sebastián.

pk-plaza-patrona-candelaria.aviso: Very busy at weekends and during religious festivals.
pk-plaza-patrona-candelaria.desc: Large paved esplanade right on the seafront, next to the Basilica of Candelaria. Reached at the end of Calle de la Arena.

pk-candelaria-centro.aviso: The fallback when it rains or the seafront is full because of the festivals.
pk-candelaria-centro.desc: Guarded private underground car park on the town's shopping street. Entrance on Calle de los Príncipes.

pk-guimar.desc: Paved council car park set up to keep traffic out of the old town, close to the town hall and the main square. Access from Avenida Obispo Pérez Cáceres.

pk-poris-abona.desc: Public roadside and bay parking facing the sea and the local swimming spots of the fishing village. Access from the motorway exit along Calle Real.

bano-valleseco-bloque.desc: Concrete solarium next to Valleseco, with steps down to the sea and a shower. One of the closest swimming spots to central Santa Cruz. There is no adapted access ramp.

charco-archile.desc: The mouth of a dry ravine forming a lagoon cut off from the sea, turquoise and very calm. A path and steps lead down. The bottom is stony: water shoes are needed.

charco-don-gabino.desc: Natural pool by Puertito de Los Silos, less busy than the main pools. Getting in and out is awkward, and it gets tricky when the tide runs strong. Water shoes are advisable.

charco-golete.desc: Small rock pool at La Caleta de Candelaria, right below the motorway. Usually empty, with free parking, though the streets down are very steep. No showers or facilities. Only when the wind and sea are calm.

charco-gomero.desc: Natural rock pools west of Garachico, unimproved and unsignposted. Hardly any tourists go there. Like the rest of the town's pools, it is not a place to enter when the sea is rough.

charco-laja-bajamar.desc: Rock pool on the Bajamar cliff, a different place from the Charco de La Laja in San Juan de la Rambla, more than 40 km away. Access is very difficult, there are no lifeguards and no route to evacuate an injured person, and there have been drownings in recent years. The sea breaks hard against the rock.

charco-roque.desc: Little-known natural pool on the Buenavista del Norte coast. It is small: when people gather there is not much room to stand. No facilities of any kind.

piscina-gigantes.desc: Seawater pool at the foot of Los Gigantes, shielded by a concrete wall. It is a dangerous spot: the rim rock is very slippery and waves have swept bathers out to open sea, with deaths in recent years. Do not sit or walk on the edge of the wall. Always check the sea state and council notices before going.

piscina-guimar.desc: Natural pool on the Güímar coast. Often low on water or dry altogether, and with no facilities at all. Worth checking its state before going; the pools on the north coast are usually in better shape.

piscina-hidalgo-norte.desc: The second pool at Punta del Hidalgo, some 500 m north of the main one. It has a shallow part and a deeper one, with metal and stone steps. Good snorkelling and views of Teide. Sharp rock: bring water shoes.

playa-abriguitos.desc: Sheltered bay next to Abades, pale sand and a gradual entry free of stones. Very clear water with fish close to shore: one of the southeast's snorkelling spots.

playa-agua-dulce.desc: Pebble beach on the Los Silos coast, mountain behind and open sea in front. Windy, with big waves. Access from the south is by very tight, steep hairpins.

playa-beril.desc: Black sand beach of around 500 m, quieter than its neighbours and with easy water access. The bottom has rock and fish, so it works well for snorkelling and for longer swims. Paid sunbeds and no public toilets.

playa-bobo.desc: Small sheltered beach in Costa Adeje. Barely any waves and pebbles underfoot, so the water sits like a natural pool. Popular with families with young children.

playa-cabezo-medano.desc: Open beach east of El Médano, one of the island's reference windsurf and kitesurf spots thanks to its steady wind. Exposed swimming on rough days.

playa-caleton-sauzal.desc: An old fishing hamlet with cave houses and a small pier. No facilities beyond a seasonal bar. The way down is a narrow winding road with no crash barriers, and you enter the water over rock. When the sea is rough you need to be a strong swimmer.

playa-candelaria.desc: Volcanic sand and pebble beach beside the Basilica of Candelaria. The only one in the town without breakwaters, so it takes the swell head-on and shrinks at high tide.

playa-castillo-pcruz.desc: Black sand beach laid out in 1990 by César Manrique alongside María Jiménez, with a landscaped promenade, cafés and a play area. Showers, toilets and sunbeds. The bottom is large stones and the swell is strong: water shoes are advisable.
playa-castillo-pcruz.cat: Black Sand Beach · Puerto de la Cruz

playa-charcada.desc: The beach of Puertito de Güímar, beside the fishing pier. Clear water and a quiet feel, with restaurants and a play area. There is another smaller beach on the far side of the village.

playa-chimisay.desc: Undeveloped beach at El Socorro de Güímar, next to the industrial estate. Rock underwater and shallow near the shore; the good entry point is sheltered and almost waveless. Plenty of parking and a restaurant right there.

playa-enramada.desc: Black volcanic sand beach next to La Caleta. Rocky patches where you enter the water. It is the landing spot for paragliders coming down off the mountain.

playa-galletas.desc: Pebble beach beside the harbour of Las Galletas. Local, barely touristy, with restaurants and a playground along the promenade. There is a sandy stretch to the right of the pier.

playa-grande-abades.desc: Pale sand and a gradual entry, little known to tourists and used mostly by local families. Usually windy with small waves, and surf schools sometimes come here. Parking for about ten cars and no toilets.

playa-guincho.desc: Fine black sand with large stones and big waves, used by surfers. Access confuses many people because it seems to run through banana plantations. The clear way is to drive down by the modern church, park there and take the footpath. Very small car park.

playa-jaca.desc: Small, very quiet beach with several rock pools and steel ladders down to the water. Windy and barely touristy, with local fishermen. A good place to watch the sunrise.

playa-jaquita-medano.desc: A string of coves and rock pools facing Montaña Roja, near El Médano. Rocky bottom, slippery entry and an uneven break. Very windy area, used for surfing.

playa-las-aguas.desc: Refurbished beach at the foot of the cliff, coarse stones rather than sand, so walking is awkward. Good swimming in summer, local feel, two restaurants alongside and few parking spaces.
playa-las-aguas.cat: Pebble Beach · San Juan de la Rambla

playa-martianez.desc: Black sand and large stones in Puerto de la Cruz, with steady north swell. Heavily used by surfers. Swimming is exposed here: respect the flags.
playa-martianez.cat: Surf Beach · Puerto de la Cruz

playa-muelle-garachico.desc: Black sand beach beside Garachico's old pier, on the lava flow of the last eruption. Stone steps drop to the water from the low wall. Parking and playground alongside.

playa-nea.desc: Roughly 300 m of coarse dark sand and pebbles in Radazul. A breakwater shields it from the swell, so the entry is gradual and free of rocks. Shower, playground and parking.

playa-pinta.desc: Small fine-sand bay beside Puerto Colón. Clear calm water with fish just a few metres from shore. Ringed by restaurants and shops.

playa-punta-fraile.desc: Black rock point with no sand, at the far northwest. Open, rough sea, not really suited to swimming or snorkelling. A quiet spot to sit and watch the sunset.

playa-punta-larga.desc: Small black pebble beach with wooden decks to lie on. Sheltered from the swell and very clear, with rock to the south where people snorkel. Used mostly by locals.

playa-radazul.desc: One of the best snorkelling spots near the capital. Two side entries sheltered from the swell and a central stairway straight into deep water. Street parking. There are no toilets and the showers are often out of order.

playa-rincon.desc: Secluded cove of roughly 400 m by 15 wide, of pebbles, gravel and black sand. Reached by dirt track and then on foot. No facilities at all, and sea conditions do not make it advisable for swimming.

playa-rojas.desc: Rocky coast with a platform of lava sand and steps down to rock pools. There is a shower. The swell is strong: fine for bathing in the pools, not for swimming out. The drive down is very narrow and steep.
playa-rojas.cat: Beach and Rock Pools · El Sauzal

playa-roques-rambla.desc: Wild cove of rock and pebble between volcanic cliffs. The sea comes in hard and it is no place to swim or to bring children. A path leads down and it closes when the swell is up.
playa-roques-rambla.cat: Wild Cove · San Juan de la Rambla

playa-san-telmo.desc: Small cove right in the centre of Puerto de la Cruz, with a jetty and a natural pool reached by ladder. Little sand and plenty of rock: good for snorkelling, with crabs and fish. Showers on site.
playa-san-telmo.cat: Beach and Rock Pool · Puerto de la Cruz

playa-socorro-guimar.desc: Sand and pebble beach in Güímar, clean and uncrowded, with very clear water and shaded areas. It is a different place from Playa El Socorro in Los Realejos, on the north coast.

playa-tabaiba.desc: Town beach at Tabaiba with a seawater pool alongside, good for children. It is a shore diving spot and there are several dive centres nearby. Parking is tight around midday.

playa-fajana-realejos.desc: Wild black-sand beach on the north of the island, inside the Rambla de Castro Protected Landscape. It is famous for the waterfall that drops straight onto the sand.
